cs.AI / 1 / 2611.29716
Fin-RSI: A Unified Library of Financial Skills, Checks, and Self-Improvement for LLM Agents
Fin-RSI：面向 LLM 智能体的金融技能、检查与自我改进统一库
Wanghao Ye, Shwai He, Sihan Chen, Yiting Wang, Bowei Tian, Guoheng Sun, Ziyi Wang, Ziyao Wang, Yexiao He, Zheyu Shen, Meng Liu, Yuning Zhang, Meng Feng, Yifei Dong, Yanhong Qian, Yang Wang, Siyuan Peng, Yilong Dai, Zhenle Duan, Joshua Liu, Lang Xiong, Aarosh Das, Zhaoyi Liu, Daeun Jung, Aditya Sarkar, Parastoo Pilevar, Xiaochuan Gong, Yancheng Zhu, Yingying Fan, Qiong Wang, Ang Li
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
As large language models (LLMs) become more capable, financial agents need tools they can readily discover and use. Yet financial software is fragmented across libraries with different interfaces and conventions, making it difficult to build reliable agent workflows. We present Fin-RSI, a unified Python library of financial skills, checks, and self-improvement designed for LLM agents. It brings together tools for market analysis, forecasting, portfolio construction, and trading research through shared interfaces across models and agent frameworks. Agents can find suitable tools from natural-language requests, reuse tested implementations, and improve generated programs through checking and feedback. Developers can extend the library with new tools without rebuilding integrations for each model. Across 20 open-weight models on six trading-position tasks, tool discovery increased the proportion of episodes producing valid programs from 9.7% to 29.2%; for models with at least 14 billion parameters, it rose from 23.6% to 64.6%. We release the library and benchmark as a shared resource for the community and plan to expand its tools and task coverage as financial agents evolve.
Chinese Translation
随着大语言模型（LLMs）能力不断增强，金融智能体需要能够轻松发现和使用的工具。然而，金融软件分散在具有不同接口和约定的库中，这使得构建可靠的智能体工作流变得困难。我们提出 Fin-RSI，一个专为 LLM 智能体设计的、包含金融技能、检查与自我改进的统一 Python 库。它通过跨模型和智能体框架的共享接口，汇集了用于市场分析、预测、投资组合构建和交易研究的工具。智能体可以从自然语言请求中找到合适的工具，复用经过测试的实现，并通过检查和反馈改进生成的程序。开发者可以用新工具扩展该库，而无需为每个模型重新构建集成。在六项交易头寸任务上对 20 个开放权重模型的测试中，工具发现将生成有效程序的回合比例从 9.7% 提高到 29.2%；对于参数量至少为 140 亿的模型，该比例从 23.6% 上升到 64.6%。我们将该库和基准作为社区的共享资源发布，并计划随着金融智能体的发展扩展其工具和任务覆盖范围。

cs.AI / 2 / 2611.29732
Reinforcement Learning from LLM-Generated (Suboptimal) Demonstrations
从大语言模型生成的（次优）演示中进行强化学习
Anurag Kadkol, Lawson L. S. Wong
cs.AI · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved substantial progress across many domains, but training an agent \textit{tabula rasa} remains highly sample-inefficient. A common remedy is to initialize the agent using a neural network pretrained on demonstrations. However, collecting demonstrations is expensive, and the demonstrations themselves can be suboptimal. In this work, we use a large language model (LLM) to generate an advice policy that produces demonstration data with effectively no human cost. We use this data to warmstart a DQN agent, and use the advice policy itself to guide exploration during training. Because LLM-generated advice is often suboptimal, we further introduce a value warmstart method that initializes the agent to recognize promising states from the advice policy's behavior, without directly copying its actions. To characterize the robustness of this method, we systematically perturb individual sub-skills of an LLM-generated advice policy for a long-horizon, sparse-reward task. Degraded advice still meaningfully accelerates learning relative to unaided baselines. These results suggest that LLM-generated advice, though suboptimal, can be a cheap alternative to costly human demonstrations.
Chinese Translation
强化学习（RL）已在许多领域取得实质性进展，但从 \textit{tabula rasa} 开始训练智能体仍然样本效率极低。一种常见的补救措施是使用在演示上预训练的神经网络来初始化智能体。然而，收集演示成本高昂，而且演示本身可能是次优的。在这项工作中，我们使用大语言模型（LLM）生成一个建议策略，该策略以实际上为零的人工成本产生演示数据。我们使用这些数据热启动一个 DQN 智能体，并使用建议策略本身在训练期间引导探索。由于 LLM 生成的建议往往是次优的，我们进一步引入一种值热启动方法，该方法初始化智能体以从建议策略的行为中识别有希望的状态，而不直接复制其动作。为了刻画该方法的鲁棒性，我们针对一个长时程、稀疏奖励任务，系统地扰动 LLM 生成建议策略的各个子技能。与无辅助的基线相比，退化的建议仍能显著加速学习。这些结果表明，LLM 生成的建议尽管次优，仍可作为昂贵人类演示的低成本替代方案。

cs.AI / 3 / 2611.29936
SAEPO: Sparse-Autoencoder-Guided Credit Assignment for Policy Optimization
SAEPO：稀疏自编码器引导的策略优化信用分配
Yusong Zhao, Zihao Zhao, Zirui Zhang, Tunyu Zhang, Ziyan Wang, Yi Wang, Chengzhi Mao, Hao Wang
cs.AI · cs.CL · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has demonstrated strong performance in improving large language model (LLM) reasoning, yet its credit-assignment signal remains coarse. Outcome verifiers provide scalable supervision by judging whether a completed response is correct, but they do not directly indicate which intermediate reasoning tokens contribute to success or failure. As a result, policy optimization can be inefficient, especially when training base models directly from sparse outcome feedback. In this paper, we introduce SAEPO, a Sparse AutoEncoder-guided token-level credit assignment method for outcome-supervised Policy Optimization. Rather than treating correctness only as a rollout-level (sequence-level) signal, SAEPO uses a pretrained sparse autoencoder (SAE) to build token-level semantic representations within reasoning trajectories; it scores each token based on the SAE concepts (e.g., penalizing wrong "final-answer" tokens but rewarding correct "reasoning-process" tokens), learned in an unsupervised manner, to achieve fine-grained credit assignment. SAEPO is a plug-in advantage-shaping module compatible with various policy optimization algorithms. We instantiate SAEPO with both GRPO and GSPO, covering token-ratio and sequence-ratio policy-gradient objectives, and evaluate SAEPO across three LLM backbones on six math and two code benchmarks. Empirical results show that SAEPO improves both the math and code benchmark averages over the matched baselines, with gains of up to 6.63% and 5.57%, respectively. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base, training curves also show faster early accuracy growth. Feature and token-level analyses suggest that the SAE-derived signal favors question-relevant concepts and reasoning tokens.
Chinese Translation
带可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）在提升大语言模型（LLM）推理能力方面已表现出强劲性能，但其信用分配信号仍然粗糙。结果验证器通过判断完整回复是否正确来提供可扩展监督，但它们并不直接指出哪些中间推理 token 对成功或失败有贡献。因此，策略优化可能效率低下，尤其是在直接利用稀疏结果反馈训练基础模型时。本文提出 SAEPO，一种面向结果监督策略优化的稀疏自编码器引导的 token 级信用分配方法。SAEPO 不再仅将正确性视为 rollout 级（序列级）信号，而是使用预训练稀疏自编码器（SAE）在推理轨迹内构建 token 级语义表示；它根据以无监督方式学习到的 SAE 概念对每个 token 打分（例如惩罚错误的“最终答案” token，但奖励正确的“推理过程” token），以实现细粒度信用分配。SAEPO 是一个即插即用的优势塑形模块，兼容多种策略优化算法。我们将 SAEPO 与 GRPO 和 GSPO 分别实例化，涵盖 token 比例和序列比例的策略梯度目标，并在六个数学和两个代码基准上跨三个 LLM 骨干模型评估 SAEPO。实证结果表明，SAEPO 在相匹配的基线上提高了数学和代码基准的平均值，分别最高提升 6.63% 和 5.57%。在 Qwen3-1.7B-Base 上，训练曲线还显示出早期准确率增长更快。特征和 token 级分析表明，SAE 衍生的信号偏向于与问题相关的概念和推理 token。

cs.AI / 4 / 2611.30042
SWAM: State-aware World Action Model for Multi-Agent 3D Environments
SWAM：面向多智能体3D环境的状态感知世界动作模型
Jenna Kang, Bingxuan Li, Colin Groth, Anatolii Evdokimov, Sai Zhang, Qi Sun
cs.AI · cs.CV
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Interactive world models generate virtual environments autoregressively from player actions and visual history. However, visual history alone cannot reliably capture the evolving states of independently acting non-player characters (NPCs) in real games, particularly when they are outside the camera view. Recent multi-agent world models address this challenge through joint multi-view generation or persistent shared state, but often rely on external observations, like maps or scene geometry, or predefined state transitions. We present SWAM, a State-aware World Action Model that separates agent-state evolution from autoregressive visual generation in interactive 3D environments. A lightweight state model propagates character dynamics from actions without consuming generated frames, combining motion priors with learned scene-dependent corrections. The predicted states then guide an autoregressive diffusion transformer alongside visual history through a novel conditioning scheme. Rather than requiring an explicit scene geometry map or visibility tests, the conditioning indicates where characters may appear, allowing the diffusion model to learn their appearance and occlusion. This design enables NPCs to evolve independently of visual generation while maintaining consistent observations across visibility changes, interactions, and respawns. Evaluations in a custom Godot-based first-person shooter game demonstrate improvements in visual fidelity, NPC consistency, and long-horizon stability over existing approaches.
Chinese Translation
交互式世界模型根据玩家动作和视觉历史自回归地生成虚拟环境。然而，仅凭视觉历史无法可靠地捕捉真实游戏中独立行动的非玩家角色（NPC）不断演变的状态，尤其是当它们处于相机视野之外时。近期的多智能体世界模型通过联合多视图生成或持久共享状态来应对这一挑战，但往往依赖外部观测（如地图或场景几何），或依赖预定义的状态转移。我们提出 SWAM，一种状态感知的世界动作模型，它在交互式3D环境中将智能体状态演化与自回归视觉生成分离。一个轻量级状态模型根据动作传播角色动力学，而不消耗生成的帧，并将运动先验与学习到的场景相关修正相结合。随后，预测状态通过一种新颖的条件化方案，与视觉历史一起引导自回归扩散Transformer。该条件化方案不要求显式的场景几何图或可见性测试，而是指示角色可能出现的位置，使扩散模型能够学习其外观和遮挡。这种设计使NPC能够独立于视觉生成进行演化，同时在可见性变化、交互和重生过程中保持一致的观测。在一个定制的基于Godot的第一人称射击游戏中的评估表明，与现有方法相比，该方法在视觉保真度、NPC一致性和长时程稳定性方面有所提升。

cs.AI / 5 / 2611.30131
iFeST: An Iterative Motion Correction Framework for Fetal Brain Diffusion MRI via Frequency-Spatial-Temporal Modeling
iFeST：一种通过频率-空间-时间建模的胎儿脑扩散MRI迭代运动校正框架
Haoan Xu, Ruike Chen, Jing Xia, Haotian Li, Huanyun Zhang, Cong Sun, Guangbin Wang, Shuhao Zhang, Zhigang Gao, Dan Wu
cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Fetal brain diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) is a pivotal non-invasive tool for assessing the development of brain connectivity and microstructure. However, the prolonged acquisition times and complex sampling requirements render dMRI highly susceptible to unpredictable fetal motion. Existing motion correction methods typically process each dMRI volume independently and focus on inter-slice motion. Such strategies fail to utilize the coherent information between dMRI volumes along different diffusion directions and lack the ability to restore the intra-slice corruption. To address these limitations, we proposed iFeST, an iterative framework that combines frequency (k-space), spatial, and temporal (inter-slice) modeling for fetal brain dMRI motion correction. At each iteration, iFeST integrates information across diffusion directions into fiber orientation distributions (FODs). These distributions encode local fiber orientations within each voxel and serve as microstructural priors for intra-slice restoration and inter-slice alignment in the next iteration. To train the framework, we developed a fetal brain dMRI motion simulator that synthesizes compound motion artifacts from FODs. Evaluation on simulated datasets demonstrated that iFeST outperformed four inter-slice networks in motion estimation and three intra-slice networks in image restoration. Further validation on a real-world dataset confirmed significantly better volume reconstruction and FOD estimation than conventional pipelines. Overall, iFeST provides a learning-based framework for fetal dMRI motion correction, restoring motion-corrupted data and improving microstructural reconstruction for downstream diagnostic applications.
Chinese Translation
胎儿脑扩散磁共振成像（dMRI）是评估脑连接性和微结构发育的关键非侵入性工具。然而，较长的采集时间和复杂的采样要求使dMRI极易受到不可预测的胎儿运动的影响。现有的运动校正方法通常独立处理每个dMRI体数据，并关注层间运动。此类策略未能利用沿不同扩散方向的dMRI体数据之间的相干信息，并且缺乏恢复层内损坏的能力。为解决这些局限性，我们提出了iFeST，这是一种迭代框架，结合了频率（k空间）、空间和时间（层间）建模，用于胎儿脑dMRI运动校正。在每次迭代中，iFeST将跨扩散方向的信息整合为纤维取向分布（FODs）。这些分布编码每个体素内的局部纤维取向，并在下一次迭代中作为层内恢复和层间对齐的微结构先验。为训练该框架，我们开发了一个胎儿脑dMRI运动模拟器，其从FODs合成复合运动伪影。在模拟数据集上的评估表明，iFeST在运动估计方面优于四种层间网络，在图像恢复方面优于三种层内网络。在真实世界数据集上的进一步验证证实，与常规流程相比，其体数据重建和FOD估计显著更好。总体而言，iFeST为胎儿dMRI运动校正提供了一个基于学习的框架，可恢复受运动损坏的数据，并改善下游诊断应用的微结构重建。

cs.AI / 6 / 2611.30134
WASP: Continual Weight Adaptation for Streaming LLM Personalization
WASP：面向流式 LLM 个性化的持续权重适应
Linxi Xie, Chonghua Liao, Mengxuan Wu, Guandao Yang, Zhangyang Wang, Kai Wang
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Personalized large language models (LLMs) should continually adapt to users' evolving preferences. Yet extracting preference changes from noisy interaction histories while supporting inexpensive updates remains challenging. We introduce WASP (Weight Adaptation for Streaming Personalization), a recurrent framework that captures fine-grained preferences directly from raw user interactions and generates personalized LoRA adapters without expensive per-user optimization. Specifically, WASP achieves this by training a shared hypernetwork that maintains a compact user representation and outputs adapter weights in a single forward pass. As new interactions arrive, WASP updates this representation without reprocessing full interaction history, enabling continual adaptation with per-update costs independent of history length. Experiments on personalization benchmarks and chronological interaction streams show that WASP sustains high-quality personalization over long horizons under fixed compute and storage budgets. Together, these results support efficient streaming personalization and facilitate privacy-preserving on-device deployment.
Chinese Translation
个性化的大语言模型（LLM）应当持续适应用户不断变化的偏好。然而，从含噪的交互历史中提取偏好变化，同时支持低成本的更新，仍然具有挑战性。我们提出 WASP（面向流式个性化的权重适应），这是一个循环框架，它直接从原始用户交互中捕获细粒度偏好，并在无需昂贵的逐用户优化的情况下生成个性化 LoRA 适配器。具体而言，WASP 通过训练一个共享超网络来实现这一点，该超网络维护一个紧凑的用户表示，并在单次前向传播中输出适配器权重。当新的交互到来时，WASP 更新该表示而无需重新处理完整的交互历史，从而实现持续适应，且每次更新的开销与历史长度无关。在个性化基准和时间顺序交互流上的实验表明，在固定的计算和存储预算下，WASP 能够在长时间跨度内维持高质量的个性化。这些结果共同支持高效的流式个性化，并有助于保护隐私的端侧部署。

cs.AI / 7 / 2611.30139
AutoSECO: Automated Skill Evolution for Cross-Problem Combinatorial Optimization with General-Purpose LLM Agents
AutoSECO：使用通用大语言模型智能体的跨问题组合优化自动化技能演化
Zirui Zhu, Cong Zhang, Ni Zhang, Kuan Xu, Zhiguang Cao
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
General-purpose large language model (LLM) agents can develop complete solvers for combinatorial optimization problems. Their specialization, however, often relies on workflows engineered for individual problems, limiting the reuse of development expertise. We propose AutoSECO, an automated skill evolution method that learns reusable solver-development guidance from experience. The challenge is that external evaluation measures the completed solver, while the skill guides decisions during development. AutoSECO connects this feedback to guidance deficiencies by tracing performance shortfalls through solver code and recorded development decisions. Revisions are expressed as general instructions and retained only if a fresh solver developed under the revised skill achieves a lower mean evaluation gap. Evolved solely on the traveling salesperson problem (TSP), the skill guides fresh agents in developing solvers for capacitated vehicle routing, job-shop scheduling, and three-dimensional bin packing without further skill evolution. On TSP, the final mean benchmark gap is 0.52\%, compared with 0.98\% for the skill-evolution baseline SkillOpt. Across all four problems, the evolved skill achieves better aggregate results than no skill guidance, the initial skill, and SkillOpt. The same frozen skill also supports solver development under alternative model--harness configurations. These findings suggest that solver-development experience can be retained as reusable expertise for general-purpose LLM agents.
Chinese Translation
通用大语言模型（LLM）智能体可以为组合优化问题开发完整的求解器。然而，它们的专门化往往依赖于为单个问题设计的工作流，从而限制了开发专业知识的复用。我们提出 AutoSECO，一种自动化技能演化方法，它从经验中学习可复用的求解器开发指导。挑战在于，外部评估衡量的是已完成的求解器，而技能则在开发过程中指导决策。AutoSECO 通过追踪求解器代码与记录的开发决策中的性能不足，将该反馈与指导缺陷联系起来。修订以通用指令的形式表达，并且仅当在修订后技能下开发的新求解器取得更低的平均评估差距时才被保留。该技能仅在旅行商问题（TSP）上演化，便能指导新智能体为带容量约束的车辆路径、作业车间调度和三维装箱开发求解器，而无需进一步的技能演化。在 TSP 上，最终平均基准差距为 0.52\%，而技能演化基线 SkillOpt 为 0.98\%。在全部四个问题上，演化后的技能相比无技能指导、初始技能和 SkillOpt 取得了更好的总体结果。同一冻结技能还支持在替代的模型—执行框架配置下进行求解器开发。这些发现表明，求解器开发经验可以作为通用 LLM 智能体的可复用专业知识被保留下来。

cs.AI / 8 / 2611.30281
Learning Heterogeneous Reasoning in Large Language Models: From Mode Compatibility to Local Bottlenecks
大语言模型中的异构推理学习：从模式兼容性到局部瓶颈
Sunbowen Li, Dandan Song, Shengkun Ma, Xuanning Cao
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Post-training large language models routinely pools reasoning trajectories from diverse teachers or algorithms, yet it remains unclear whether standard supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can learn such heterogeneous strategies without explicit mode conditioning. We study the learnability and local bottlenecks of heterogeneous reasoning through a formal mixture formulation and controlled experiments. We first formalize the representational compatibility of the optimal autoregressive model with latent reasoning mixtures: the target next-token distribution weights modes by their prefix posteriors and concentrates on a single mode once alternative modes assign negligible likelihood to the prefix. In a verifiable symbolic graph-search environment with paired breadth-first and depth-first search trajectories, no consistent disadvantage is observed for unlabeled mixed SFT relative to homogeneous or labeled baselines under matched token budgets while preserving both modes. Scaling across 0.6B--14B models and data budgets largely eliminates global mode confusion, shifting the primary bottleneck to local state-tracking transitions. Because a local mistake affects the final outcome only when subsequent reasoning is sensitive to that step, we find that only a small fraction of local errors are outcome-determining \emph{Critical Reasoning Nodes (CRNs)}, and that single-step repairs at these nodes rescue failing trajectories across symbolic search and natural language benchmarks whenever the model has sufficient downstream competence to complete the remaining derivation. Our environment is open-sourced at https://github.com/Bowen1911/Symbolic_graph_env.
Chinese Translation
大语言模型的后训练通常会汇集来自不同教师或算法的推理轨迹，但标准监督微调（SFT）能否在没有显式模式条件的情况下学习这种异构策略，仍不清楚。我们通过形式化的混合建模与受控实验，研究异构推理的可学习性与局部瓶颈。我们首先形式化最优自回归模型与潜在推理混合之间的表示兼容性：目标下一词元分布按各模式的前缀后验对其加权，并且一旦其他模式对前缀赋予可忽略的似然，该分布就集中到单一模式上。在一个具有成对广度优先与深度优先搜索轨迹的可验证符号图搜索环境中，在匹配词元预算且保留两种模式的条件下，相对于同质或带标签的基线，无标签混合 SFT 未观察到一致的劣势。在 0.6B--14B 模型和数据预算上的扩展很大程度上消除了全局模式混淆，将主要瓶颈转移到局部的状态跟踪转移上。由于局部错误只有在后续推理对该步骤敏感时才会影响最终结果，我们发现只有一小部分局部错误是决定结果的 \emph{关键推理节点（CRNs）}，并且只要模型具备足够的后续能力来完成剩余推导，在这些节点上进行单步修复就能在符号搜索和自然语言基准上挽救失败的轨迹。我们的环境已开源于 https://github.com/Bowen1911/Symbolic_graph_env。

mini-psych-agent: Evaluating Human-Like Behavior in LLM Agents through Interactive Psychological Environments
mini-psych-agent：通过交互式心理学环境评估 LLM 智能体的类人行为
Yi-Fei Cao, Tianxin Huang, Hanbo Xie, Jian-Qiao Zhu
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
A Large Language Model (LLM), its harness, and the test-time compute budget jointly determine its behavior. Consequently, the same underlying model, embedded in different agentic workflows or allocated different amounts of test-time compute, can exhibit markedly different performance. Psychologists face an analogous challenge when evaluating human performance: the same person may behave differently under different incentives and levels of deliberation. Psychological tasks therefore provide an ideal testbed for studying such behavioral variation. However, when adapted to LLMs, these tasks are typically text-transcribed, replaying fixed, language-rendered experiments as static prompts. This format is ill-suited to agent evaluation, where actions can alter future observations and task states. Conversely, although dynamic environments are prevalent in the evaluation of LLM agents, they rarely ask whether the resulting behavior is human-like. Here, we bridge this gap by transforming psychological tasks into dynamic environments in which agents can interact and by using a learned human-policy model to evaluate how compatible the resulting behavioral trajectories are with human behavior. Across these environments, we find that this compatibility varies with an LLM's agentic configuration and the psychological task, and that memory raises it mainly by making choices more predictable rather than more human-like. These findings motivate a more holistic evaluation of LLM agents in psychology-inspired environments, accounting for both the backbone model and its agentic scaffold.

大型语言模型（LLM）、其运行框架以及测试时计算预算共同决定了它的行为。因此，同一个底层模型在嵌入不同的智能体工作流或被分配不同数量的测试时计算资源时，可能表现出显著不同的性能。心理学家在评估人类表现时面临着类似的挑战：同一个人在不同的激励和不同程度的审慎思考下可能表现出不同的行为。因此，心理学任务为研究此类行为差异提供了理想的试验平台。然而，当这些任务被改编用于 LLM 时，它们通常被转录为文本，以静态提示的形式重放固定的、以语言呈现的实验。这种形式不适合智能体评估，因为在智能体评估中，动作可以改变未来的观察和任务状态。相反，尽管动态环境在 LLM 智能体的评估中很普遍，但它们很少追问由此产生的行为是否类人。在此，我们通过将心理学任务转化为智能体可以交互的动态环境，并使用学习得到的人类策略模型来评估由此产生的行为轨迹与人类行为的兼容程度，从而弥合这一差距。在这些环境中，我们发现这种兼容性随 LLM 的智能体配置和心理学任务而变化，并且记忆提升这种兼容性主要是通过使选择更可预测，而非更类人。这些发现促使人们在受心理学启发的环境中对 LLM 智能体进行更整体的评估，同时考虑骨干模型及其智能体外壳。

TamperCert: A Benchmark for Detecting Text Tampering in Degree Certificates
TamperCert：用于检测学位证书中文本篡改的基准
ChiFung Kwan, Kangzhong Wang, Youqian Zhang, Weijie Chen, Jiaqi Gao, Yongjian Wu, Eugene Yujun Fu, Qingqing Ye, Haibo Hu
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Degree certificates play a critical role in high-stakes decisions such as university admission, immigration, and hiring. The issuing institution vouches for the holder, so a forged certificate may let its bearer pass these checks. Degree certificate forgery is increasingly prevalent. Yet, many assume that it is easy to spot. Reported cases show otherwise: in 2024, the business school of the University of Hong Kong found that about 30 master's students had enrolled with forged academic credentials. Few studies have looked at how to detect forged degree certificates, partly because public benchmarks are scarce. We present TamperCert, a benchmark built from 400 real degree certificates issued by 38 universities. Each certificate was subjected to 11 publicly available tampering methods to alter the holder's name and further processed with four additional post-processing techniques, resulting in over 20,000 forged images. We evaluate 13 detectors, a commercial multimodal large language model (MLLM), and detectors trained on TamperCert.Our findings reveal that no detector is reliable for every tampering method. Consequently, a determined forger may still evade detection. Moreover, the commercial MLLM misses most forgeries made by general-purpose generative models, and post-processing, such as resizing an image or photographing it with a camera, severely degrades detection.

Revisiting LLMs as Context Engineers
重新审视作为上下文工程师的 LLMs
Junrui Zhang, Zeyu Xu, Runchuan Zhu, Jie Peng, Long Zhang, Zixin Ding, Jiaxin Lin, Kai Wang, Jianmin Ji, Junyuan Hong
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
As large language models (LLMs) are used in more and more new tasks, context engineering becomes a fundamental method to efficiently steer LLMs by constructing instruction prompts or metadata without intensive training. A growing number of LLM context engineering (LCE) approaches automate the task by casting the LLM itself as the engineer that draws generalizable instructions or experiences from offline trials as context. Although these methods resemble how humans learn from experiences, it remains unclear \textbf{when and how} LLMs can engineer effective context from data. To answer the question, we first establish a benchmark composed of datasets with different reasoning patterns. We compared different LCE methods with different LLM families in 8B size, showing that there is no single winner for all tasks, even compared with simple baselines like chain-of-thought. Even when scaling model capabilities via more parameters or generation iterations, LCEs do not consistently boost existing performance. Across all datasets and models, the performance gains of LCEs are negatively correlated ($r=-0.5, p\le 0.05$) with the diversity of the failure modes of reasoning trajectories. Investigating how LCEs work, we find that (1) the improvement in instruction adherence can explain some success of LCEs; (2) one major bottleneck is whether LLMs can extract effective experiences out of natively diverse failures. Through this study, we uncover the limited capabilities of LCEs in abstracting principled contexts from diverse failure modes and understand how LCEs work, providing guidelines for future work.

随着大语言模型（LLMs）被用于越来越多新的任务，上下文工程成为一种基本方法，通过构建指令提示或元数据而无需密集训练来高效引导 LLMs。越来越多的 LLM 上下文工程（LCE）方法通过将 LLM 自身设定为工程师、从离线试验中提取可泛化的指令或经验作为上下文，来自动化这一任务。尽管这些方法类似于人类从经验中学习的方式，但 LLMs \textbf{何时以及如何}能够从数据中工程化出有效上下文仍不清楚。为回答该问题，我们首先建立了一个由具有不同推理模式的数据集组成的基准。我们在 8B 规模下比较了不同 LCE 方法与不同 LLM 家族，结果表明没有任何一种方法能在所有任务上胜出，即使与思维链等简单基线相比也是如此。即使通过更多参数或生成迭代来扩展模型能力，LCEs 也不能持续提升现有性能。在所有数据集和模型上，LCEs 的性能增益与推理轨迹失败模式的多样性呈负相关（$r=-0.5, p\le 0.05$）。在研究 LCEs 如何工作时，我们发现：（1）指令遵循性的提升可以解释 LCEs 的部分成功；（2）一个主要瓶颈在于 LLMs 能否从本质上多样的失败中提取有效经验。通过这项研究，我们揭示了 LCEs 在从多样失败模式中抽象出有原则的上下文方面的能力有限，并理解了 LCEs 如何工作，为未来工作提供了指导。

Reproducible by Seed? Not on GPUs: Batch-Dependent Non-Determinism in Text-to-Image Models
靠种子就能复现？在 GPU 上并非如此：文本到图像模型中的批次依赖非确定性
Javier Conde, Xiuyuan Qi, Shanshan Liu, Pedro Reviriego
cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
In text to image AI models, fixing the prompt and the random seed is widely assumed to fix the image. We show that it does not on GPUs. We evaluate six text-to-image models (diffusion and autoregressive) under four numerical precisions and quantizations on three GPU types (RTX A6000, RTX 6000 Ada, and H100 NVL), across up to 100 prompts per set for all six models. For each configuration we compare, with the prompt and seed fixed, the image generated alone with the image generated inside a batch, and we also compare across GPUs. Every replay control reported here is bit-exact, so the variation is not random noise: the execution setting, mainly the batch composition and the GPU, decides the output. The effect is large and model dependent. Structural similarity between the single-image and the batched output falls to 0.580 for an autoregressive model in bf16 and to 0.551 with int8. For a second autoregressive model in bf16 it falls to 0.261 with sampled decoding and to 0.229 with greedy decoding, and for an fp8 diffusion model to 0.68. A diffusion model in bf16 stays close to the batch-1 output (0.96-0.98) but changes every image. In most cases the batched image is a different but equally valid image; in some, such as prompts with digits and counters, it is visibly worse. Cross-GPU differences are of the same order as the batch effect: for one autoregressive model in bf16 compared across two GPU architectures (RTX 6000 Ada versus RTX A6000), no image is bit-identical and the cross-GPU LPIPS (0.355 to 0.383) matches the batch effect within one GPU (0.347 to 0.381). The consequences are direct: seeds do not make results reproducible, benchmarks and image-quality comparisons that mix batch sizes or hardware can be biased, and safety audits and A/B tests on generated images need the serving setup reported.

在文本到图像 AI 模型中，固定提示词和随机种子被广泛认为就能固定图像。我们表明，在 GPU 上并非如此。我们在三类 GPU（RTX A6000、RTX 6000 Ada 和 H100 NVL）上，在四种数值精度与量化设置下评估了六个文本到图像模型（扩散模型和自回归模型），对全部六个模型，每组最多使用 100 个提示词。对于每种配置，我们在固定提示词和种子的情况下，将单独生成的图像与在批次内生成的图像进行比较，并且还跨 GPU 进行比较。这里报告的每个重放对照都是逐位精确的，因此这种变化不是随机噪声：执行设置——主要是批次组成和 GPU——决定了输出。该效应很大且依赖于模型。对于 bf16 下的一个自回归模型，单张图像输出与批次输出之间的结构相似性降至 0.580，而在 int8 下降至 0.551。对于 bf16 下的第二个自回归模型，在采样解码下它降至 0.261，在贪心解码下降至 0.229；而对于一个 fp8 扩散模型，则降至 0.68。一个 bf16 下的扩散模型与批次大小为 1 的输出保持接近（0.96–0.98），但会改变每一张图像。在大多数情况下，批次中的图像是一张不同但同样有效的图像；在某些情况下，例如包含数字和计数器的提示词，它明显更差。跨 GPU 差异与批次效应处于同一量级：对于 bf16 下的一个自回归模型，在两种 GPU 架构（RTX 6000 Ada 与 RTX A6000）之间进行比较时，没有任何图像是逐位相同的，并且跨 GPU 的 LPIPS（0.355 至 0.383）与同一 GPU 内的批次效应（0.347 至 0.381）相当。后果是直接的：种子并不能使结果可复现，混合不同批次大小或硬件的基准测试和图像质量比较可能产生偏差，而针对生成图像的安全审计和 A/B 测试需要报告服务配置。

cs.AI / 13 / 2611.30662
WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce
WeMM-Ecom：推进面向微信电商的多模态内容理解
Binhui Xie, Jinmin Li, Haomiao Tang, Guangting Wang, Song Jin, Jianwei Zhu, Fengyun Rao, Jing Lyu
cs.AI · cs.CV
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
We present WeMM-Ecom, a family of multimodal large language models that deliver frontier e-commerce capabilities while achieving state-of-the-art general-purpose performance at their respective scales. The family spans five sizes, from a 0.8B dense model to a 35B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters. Our training pipeline begins with two-stage continued pre-training that progressively raises the proportion of e-commerce data within a diverse multimodal data mixture, followed by hybrid-thinking post-training that combines on-policy distillation and reinforcement learning to support both non-thinking and thinking modes. For evaluation, we construct a comprehensive suite of 28 e-commerce benchmarks (23 in-house and five open-source) covering eight business scenarios and complement it with 64 public general-purpose benchmarks. On the e-commerce suite, WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B surpasses substantially larger open-source flagship models, including Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, HY4, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. On the general-purpose suite, every WeMM-Ecom model surpasses its similarly sized Qwen3.5 counterpart, with the lightweight variants (e.g., WeMM-Ecom-2B) showing clear advantages over leading lightweight models such as Qwen3.5-2B, MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B, and LFM3-VL-2B. Beyond benchmarks, WeMM-Ecom now powers hundreds of production use cases in WeChat, including catalog management, multimodal product search, and livestream commerce, serving billion-scale requests per day. We publicly release all model weights and detail our data curation, training recipe, and benchmark construction to facilitate future work on domain-specialized multimodal models. We have released the model weights and code to facilitate future research at https://github.com/Tencent/WeMM-Ecom.

Uncovering Hidden Behaviours in Language Models via Limited-Parameter Finetuning
通过有限参数微调揭示语言模型中的隐藏行为
Boyd Kane, Jo J. Jiao, Elizabeth Donoway, Bryce Woodworth, Alex Cloud, Alexander M. Turner
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models can have behaviours which only arise in hard-to-anticipate contexts. These hidden behaviours pose a challenge to alignment audits, which seek to uncover problematic model behaviour but are limited by the scenarios the auditor can anticipate. To address this challenge, we explore limited-parameter finetuning (LPF) on examples of a target behaviour. While training 3-25% of LoRA parameters, LPF reveals whether the model has a hidden behaviour, even when standard behavioural evaluations cannot. LPF succeeds on a suite of model organisms with hidden behaviours (8-14B parameters), and also surfaces naturally occurring hidden behaviours in open-weight models (27-35B parameters). LPF can thus distinguish between models which appear behaviourally identical to an auditor, and does not require the context in which the hidden behaviour surfaces. LPF provides a novel affordance that may be useful for auditing frontier AI models. However, we do not evaluate LPF against baselines in a realistic auditing setting, so further work is needed to determine its practicality.

Transport-Safe Evaluation of LLM Agents: Trajectory-Dependent Judge Error and Anytime-Valid Auditing
LLM 智能体的迁移安全评估：依赖轨迹的评判器误差与随时有效审计
Yulliwas Ameur, Samia Bouzefrane, Soumya Banerjee
cs.AI · stat.ME
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) agents are often ranked by an LLM judge whose error rates are measured once and reused for every agent. The corrected success rates can then be biased when the judge's errors depend on the trajectory and agents differ in the trajectories they produce for successes or failures. We derive the exact asymptotic bias and give a chain of checks from identification to simultaneous ranks. On a four-agent semi-synthetic benchmark, a scalar correction with oracle calibration has maximum bias 0.245 and mean pointwise coverage 0.016, and never recovers the full ranking (0/250 replications). Augmented inverse-probability weighting (AIPW) with a uniform or a design-aware random audit keeps the maximum bias below 0.003, with mean pointwise coverage of 0.939 and 0.950. In a 48-cell stress test, effective target support rises only from 0.209 to 0.805 as calibration grows from 600 to 4,800 labels, while audited AIPW keeps a mean absolute error of 0.018-0.020. Without calibration support, or with judge dependence within an externally justified bound, we report valid bounds or sensitivity sets and carry them into rank sets. An e-process confidence sequence stays valid, for a stable target, under predictable adaptive auditing and arbitrary stopping.

large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Laypeople increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for triage advice, but LLMs answer in variable free text, which makes it hard to evaluate them for use in medical devices. Decision models, which assign a probability to each predefined triage category, may be easier to evaluate. To test their triage accuracy, we evaluated 16 decision models (14 open-weight, 2 proprietary) on 233 synthetic and 10,000 real-world cases, yielding 163,728 total assessments. The best models triaged 72.1% of synthetic cases correctly and agreed with an existing algorithm in 56.1% of real-world cases. They were more promising for recognising emergencies early: given only demographics, chief complaints, risk factors and red-flag answers, the best model reached an AUROC of 0.87. At a 5% error margin, it could decide for or against emergencies for about half of users. Decision models should therefore not replace triage engines but could shorten symptom assessments at setting-specific error margins.

Abstract
In agriculture, typically over half of the applied nitrogen fertiliser is lost to water and to air. Precision fertilisation aims to reduce these losses while maintaining yield and quality, yet existing tools struggle to capture farm-specific challenges in determining optimal nitrogen rates. Static recommendations are common and overlook on-farm constraints, such as delays due to weather or machinery availability, or change in budgets. Each constraint governs when and how growers apply fertiliser in practice. Here we present a grower-in-the-loop framework for winter wheat in England, combining baseline fertilisation planning from a machine learning-derived nitrogen-response curve with in-season adaptation via a large language model. We evaluated the framework using data from long-term experiments (LTEs), replicated field trials, and farm deployments. Retrospective model validation using LTEs confirmed low economic decision-loss across multiple seasons. Using field and farm trials, baseline schedules were shown to match standard-practice yields with less nitrogen, whereas in-season adjusted schedules additionally retained grain quality standards. Given this enhanced performance, in-season adaptation absorbed weather, machinery and budget constraints to keep recommendations executable. The framework therefore shows promise for translating static recommendations into adaptable, grower-informed decisions for sustainable fertiliser management.

Abstract
Annually 1.9 million deaths and 89.7 million disability-adjusted life years are caused by exposure to agents during work (e.g., welding fumes, silica dust, and noise pollution). To improve worker health, high-quality exposure assessments are crucial. Therefore, free-text job descriptions from large-scale occupational cohorts are manually standardized through occupational classifications and linked to hazardous exposures using Job Exposure Matrices (JEM). However, manual coding is slow, unreliable (i.e., 44-89% inter-coder reliability), and costly, due to i) short, ambiguous free-text job descriptions, ii) classifications containing hundreds to thousands of categories, and iii) the absence of gold standards. With 46%-79% accuracy, state-of-the-art automatic occupational coding tools achieve classification performance on human level. However, their performance drops to 17-26% on out-of-distribution datasets. Furthermore, their supervised architectures limit them to occupational classifications present in the training set. Consequently, JEM using other classifications are incompatible, leaving vital exposure-response associations unexplored. Our Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework, OPERAG, enables classification into any occupational classification without expert-labelled databases. It retrieves coding index information and combines this with Large Language Model-based classification. Validated on AsiaLymph's 36,062 real-world job descriptions, OPERAG achieved 42.6% occupational classification accuracy on the 4th coding level, substantially outperforming existing tools and approaching human coders' 51-56% inter-coder reliability. Using two JEM named ALOHA+ and SHOCK, 89.9-98.6% accuracy was achieved on exposure assessment. OPERAG approaches human-level, universal occupational classification, enabling efficient and effective large-scale exposure assessment to improve worker health.

cs.AI

大语言模型相关
Abstract
Efficient vehicle routing is critical to logistics and transportation, yet solving large-scale capacitated vehicle routing problems (CVRP) remains computationally challenging due to their combinatorial complexity. One approach to solve large-scale vehicle routing optimization is to identify promising subproblems and then optimize them using solvers. In this paper, we propose a framework of automatic heuristic design (AHD) in which a large language model (LLM) autonomously refines heuristics for selecting subproblems, enabling effective optimization of large-scale CVRP instances. Compared to prior approaches that train task-specific neural networks to select among heuristically constructed subproblems, our method discovers generalizable, interpretable LLM-generated heuristics to directly construct subproblems. Experiments show that our approach achieves comparable in-distribution performance while outperforming neural network-based policies on out-of-distribution instances with large-scale problems.

Making Protocol Effects Explicit: LLM-to-Packet Simulation for Superpod Interconnect Exploration
使协议效应显式化：面向 Superpod 互连探索的 LLM-to-Packet 仿真
Yu Zhu, Xinhao Yang, Zhaoshi Li, Baodong Wu, Boxun Li, Wenxue Li, Guohao Dai, Hongyang Jia, Shuwen Deng, Huazhong Yang, Yuan Xie, Zhenhua Zhu, Yu Wang
cs.AR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) have become the foundation of modern AI services. The rapid growth of LLM sizes and context lengths has exceeded the memory capacity of a single GPU or NPU, requiring model partitioning across devices. However, partitioning models across devices introduces costly communication overhead, driving the need for superpods with large-scale, high-bandwidth, low-latency scale-up fabrics. Exploring superpod designs requires accurate interconnect simulation, as communication latency is jointly determined by link technologies, topologies, and scale-up protocol-stack choices. Latency-bandwidth models estimate communication latency using a startup term and a transfer term derived from message size and effective bandwidth. But they fail to capture contention and protocol effects. Packet-level simulators like ns-3 model routing, queueing, and packet timing, but require protocol-specific LLM-to-packet implementations. This paper presents ProtoBridge, an ns-3-based LLM-to-packet simulator for superpod interconnect exploration. To make protocol effects explicit, ProtoBridge introduces two abstraction layers over ns-3: (1) an operation-to-packet (OTP) layer that captures protocol-specific packet exchanges and dependencies, and (2) a packet-execution (PEX) layer that applies shared packet-level mechanisms to the ns-3 event system. ProtoBridge achieves average latency error of 17.8\% on H200 NVLink4 and 10.3\% on C500 MetaXLink. To enable faster superpod evaluation for further interconnect exploration, we derive a surrogate model that combines OTP parameters with analytical models of PEX mechanisms. The surrogate reduces evaluation time from 2.38$\sim$75.70s to 20.5us per operation. We use ProtoBridge to analyze two emerging superpod designs, scale-up memory pool and co-packaged optics (CPO) interconnects, revealing design insights for future LLM superpod architectures.

ANOR: Scaling Sparse Attention with a GPU-PNM Computing Hierarchy
ANOR：利用 GPU-PNM 计算层级扩展稀疏注意力
Hyunsu Ye, Hyunmin Choi, Jaehong Cho, Jaeseo Lee, Hyeongseok Gwak, Joohee Lee, Donguk Moon, Woosuk Chung, Hoshik Kim, Kiwan Maeng, Jongse Park
cs.AR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Serving large language models with long contexts requires keeping the key-value (KV) cache of every request, which can exceed GPU memory capacity. Sparse attention reads only a small, query-dependent subset of this cache at each decoding step, yet must retain the full cache because later steps may select other entries. Processing-near-memory (PNM) devices attached through Compute Express Link (CXL) can hold the full cache and compute attention where it resides. Prior GPU-PNM systems for sparse attention are PNM-centric, processing most of the attention on the PNM. As existing CXL-PNM devices provide far less memory bandwidth than GPU HBM, this PNM-centric execution makes the PNM the bottleneck and leaves the GPU idle waiting for attention results. We present ANOR, a GPU-PNM joint acceleration system that exploits the selection locality of sparse attention by computing most of the attention on the GPU from a cache of recently selected entries and processing only the misses on the PNM. As the PNM processes cache misses directly, GPU cache updates can be decoupled from current-step execution. We develop a bounded cache-update policy that limits updates to the point where the hit ratio of later steps saturates, reducing GPU-facing link traffic. We add a small on-chip Early Streaming Buffer (ESB) that captures KV data during PNM attention and streams it to the GPU, avoiding most redundant DRAM reads despite the bandwidth mismatch between PNM memory and the GPU-facing link. We also propose an adaptive cache-factor mechanism that adjusts GPU cache size to the serving load, balancing hit ratio and batch size. Across two models and three long-context agentic workloads, ANOR improves decode throughput by 2.3x over HiSparse and 2.0x over a PNM baseline on average. These results show that PNM is most effective not as the primary attention engine but as a computing tier of the GPU memory hierarchy.

cs.AR / 22 / 2611.30766
Bridging the Semantic Gap from Natural Language Specifications to RTL with Layered Formal Guidance
以分层形式化引导弥合从自然语言规范到 RTL 的语义鸿沟
Yan Tan, Xiangchen Meng, Yangdi Lyu
cs.AR · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
While large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in generating register-transfer level (RTL) code from natural-language specifications, their reliability remains limited on designs with complex control logic and temporal behavior. This stems from a fundamental semantic gap: high-level natural language often leaves implementation-critical details underspecified, forcing LLMs to infer unstated assumptions. This paper presents Layered Formal Guidance, a novel framework that bridges this semantic gap by using formal properties as an intermediate semantic layer between natural-language specifications and RTL generation. Our framework applies formal guidance across three layers: property-driven specification augmentation before generation, property-consistency checking after generation, and counterexample-guided refinement after checking. Experiments on RTLLM benchmarks and various open-source IP designs demonstrate that our framework achieves higher functional correctness and lower sampled output-trace diversity. Furthermore, we show that Layered Formal Guidance can flexibly augment both general-purpose LLMs and domain-specific models to substantially improve their generation reliability.

Fadel M. Megahed, Ying-Ju Chen, Yamin Dahwich, Zhao-Wei Chen, Lucas K. Hung, Arthur Carvalho, L. Allison Jones-Farmer, Ibrahim Yousif, Inez M. Zwetsloot
cs.CE · cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
In this expository paper, we explain how quality engineers can use large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) for structured data extraction. We introduce the relevant concepts, discuss structured extraction from a measurement-system perspective, and demonstrate its implementation in R and Python. We then present two freely available web-based applications (apps): (a) extracting information from automotive recall notices and (b) monitoring quality engineering research on arXiv. To ensure the accuracy of our AI-driven structured extraction, human evaluators validated the results. In the first app, four reviewers assessed information extracted from 30 recall notices using two models, with 98.6% of the 720 field-level ratings judged fully correct. In the second app, 21 authors evaluated information extracted from 45 of their arXiv papers. All paper summaries were rated mostly correct or correct, although the evaluations identified problems with some classification fields and mathematical expressions. These results demonstrate the practical potential of structured data extraction while emphasizing the need to validate the extracted information. We make both apps and their source code publicly available so that readers can adapt the approach to their own applications.

在这篇解释性论文中，我们说明质量工程师如何使用大型语言模型（LLMs）和视觉-语言模型（VLMs）进行结构化数据提取。我们介绍相关概念，从测量系统的视角讨论结构化提取，并演示其在R和Python中的实现。然后，我们介绍两个可免费使用的基于网络的应用程序（apps）：(a) 从汽车召回通知中提取信息，以及 (b) 监测arXiv上的质量工程研究。为确保我们由AI驱动的结构化提取的准确性，人工评估者验证了结果。在第一个应用程序中，四位审阅者使用两个模型评估了从30份召回通知中提取的信息，其中720个字段级评分中有98.6%被判定为完全正确。在第二个应用程序中，21位作者评估了从他们的45篇arXiv论文中提取的信息。所有论文摘要的评分均为基本正确或正确，尽管评估发现了某些分类字段和数学表达式的问题。这些结果展示了结构化数据提取的实际潜力，同时强调了验证所提取信息的必要性。我们将这两个应用程序及其源代码公开提供，以便读者能够将该方法适配到自己的应用中。

cs.LG / 24 / 2611.31211
Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates
验证 PDE 求解器的输出：从有限元到神经代理模型
Konstantinos Dovelos
cs.CE · cs.LG · math.NA
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Physics simulation outputs increasingly come from solvers that no expert inspects, such as third-party packages in automated pipelines, programs written by large language models (LLMs), and learned surrogates. In earlier work on cardiac pulsed field ablation, we proposed that solvers return a certificate with their answers. The certificate consists of an admissible potential and an exactly charge-conserving current, and a small independent checker turns it into guaranteed error bounds against a written specification of the physics. Here, the same checker verifies the outputs of other solvers on the same problem. Specifically, FEniCSx computes both fields and receives the same bounds as our own solver. Five plausible bugs in a correct solver, one of them about 0.2% from the true impedance, all converge and pass a grid convergence study, yet the certificate rejects or refutes all five. Of three solvers written by LLMs, one is correct and certified to 0.1%, and one never solves the equation but converges. Neural networks that predict the coefficients of a reduced basis emit admissible fields and receive valid per-prediction bounds, at most 0.0021% wide inside their training range and 0.3-25% wide outside it, where 90% conformal intervals cover none of 14 tests. Untuned Fourier neural operators with free nodal outputs receive valid but uninformative bounds. On a uniform grid, interpolation onto the certificate grid limits them, and on the certificate grid, thin cells turn small nodal errors into large energy errors. Energy-norm training narrows the certified interval tenfold, and projecting the nodal-loss outputs onto the reduced basis narrows it by two to four orders of magnitude, still uninformative. The guarantee concerns the stated model and holds for any output, wherever its input lies. It is informative only when the output is accurate in energy on a grid that resolves the problem.

Sánchez, Feijóo, or Abascal? Speaker Attribution and Ideological Congruence in LLM Personas Reading Posts on X of the Leaders of the Three Main Parties of the 29N General Election in Spain
桑切斯、费霍还是阿巴斯卡尔？LLM 人设阅读西班牙 29N 大选三大主要政党领导人的 X 帖子时的说话者归因与意识形态一致性
Víctor Yeste, Candida Maria Greco, Paolo Rosso, Andrea Tagarelli
cs.CL · cs.CY · cs.SI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Source cues are central to political communication, yet reception studies with large language model (LLM) personas as synthetic audiences have not tested whether personas respond to who speaks and not only to what is said. With Spain's general election of 29 November 2026 in mind, we run a speaker-attribution experiment using 1,075 anonymised X posts by the leaders of PSOE, PP and VOX on four topics (the economy and employment, household costs, immigration and corruption) and 791 distinct value-grounded, LLM-generated personas. Each post was assigned to 300 topic-selected persona profiles, 150 grounded in the Inglehart-Welzel cultural map and 150 in Moral Foundations Theory, under four conditions: no author, Sánchez, Feijóo or Abascal, yielding 322,470 complete persona-post quartets. Naming any leader lowered support for identical text, with the penalty for Abascal nearly twice as large as those for Sánchez and Feijóo. The penalty follows the persona's elicited left-right self-placement (ideological congruence): left personas spare Sánchez and right personas spare Feijóo, although ideology was never in the message-evaluation prompt. Corruption posts were penalised under every name, whereas on other topics the ideologically closest leader generally produced little or no penalty. The leader order matches public opinion in 48 CIS barometers (2022-2026) in all three groups and the sign of all twelve differences, but fits barometers before the model's 2024 knowledge cutoff better than recent ones. Our findings demonstrate that LLM personas evaluate political speakers through systematic, value-congruent priors: however, while they replicate human candidate rank-orders across survey barometers, this alignment is ordinal rather than quantitative, highlighting their utility for controlled source-effect experiments though not as substitutes for empirical public opinion surveys.

cs.CL / 26 / 2611.29909
Training-Free Interventions for Hallucination in Large Language Models
大型语言模型幻觉的免训练干预
Can Huang
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
A frozen language model can give a wrong answer because a fact is unavailable, a reliable passage is ignored, or an unsupported claim survives generation. We review 116 works on inference-time hallucination intervention and its foundations. We trace the development from retrieval and controllable generation to methods that act on input evidence, token scores, internal representations, completed claims, or the decision to answer. For each family we compare its source of evidence, model access, preparation cost, and the task on which a correction can be established. For activation steering, we distinguish estimating a subspace from applying a state-dependent edit and separate interventions on the prompt from those on the generated prefix. Published comparisons show why faithfulness to a source, factual correctness, informativeness, and answer coverage must be measured separately. Applications in time-sensitive question answering, document synthesis, and visual grounding identify when source authority, evidence availability, or capability preservation limits a reported gain.

The Answer Is Not the State: Trajectory-Level Corrigibility in Diffusion Language Models
答案并非状态：扩散语言模型中的轨迹级可纠正性
Junchi Liao, Wentao Li
cs.CL
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion language models generate tokens at many positions on a shared canvas, making unfinished responses appear revisable. We find a counterexample: after the final answer is reopened, previously generated rationale can reconstruct the old decision despite newly available evidence. We isolate this effect by comparing reopening the answer alone with reopening both rationale and answer, and by exchanging rationales between paired trajectories. On a 150-question source-disjoint benchmark, reopening both regions makes decisions follow the evidence currently present--whether correct or deliberately corrupted--across Dream, LLaDA, and iLLaDA. On a new 100-question free-form short-answer evaluation, the same effect remains strong in LLaDA and iLLaDA but is negligible in Dream. Coherent transplanted rationales steer rebuilt decisions, while token-level attribution improves which positions to reopen without producing a compact repair. Corrigibility therefore depends on retained rationale state, not answer openness alone.

扩散语言模型在共享画布上的许多位置生成词元，使未完成的回答看起来可修订。我们发现了一个反例：在最终答案被重新打开后，尽管有新可用的证据，先前生成的推理依据仍能重建旧决策。我们通过比较仅重新打开答案与同时重新打开推理依据和答案，以及在成对轨迹之间交换推理依据，来隔离这一效应。在一个包含150个问题、来源不相交的基准上，同时重新打开两个区域使决策遵循当前存在的证据——无论该证据是正确的还是被故意污染的——这在Dream、LLaDA和iLLaDA上均成立。在一个新的包含100个问题的自由形式短答案评估中，同样的效应在LLaDA和iLLaDA中依然很强，但在Dream中可以忽略不计。连贯的移植推理依据会引导重建后的决策，而词元级归因改善了应重新打开哪些位置，却没有产生一种紧凑的修复。因此，可纠正性取决于保留的推理依据状态，而不仅仅是答案的开放性。

When 1+1 $\neq$ 2: Benchmarking Civil-Time Reasoning in Large Language Models
当 1+1 $\neq$ 2：对大型语言模型中民用时间推理的基准测试
Melika Shirian, Kianoosh Vadaei, Arshia Hemmat, Mohammad Hossein Shaker Ardakani, Ali Mamanpoosh, Matin Moqadas, Amirmasoud Rismanchian, Afsaneh Fatemi
cs.CL · cs.AI · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Calendar arithmetic is non-linear. When 1:59 AM + 1 minute occurs during daylight saving spring-forward, the result is 3:00 AM, not 2:00 AM, as the hour is skipped. We introduce CivilTime-Bench, a benchmark for civil-time reasoning covering daylight saving transitions, non-hour offsets, date-line crossings, and ISO week boundaries. With 60,011 training and 10,500 evaluation examples under strict output-contract evaluation, we benchmark seven LLMs (six instruction-tuned models and Llama-3.1-8B base) and find: zero-shot exact match varies substantially across models, contract-aware prompting often improves format compliance but yields inconsistent accuracy gains, few-shot in-context learning provides model-dependent improvements, and fine-tuning achieves 74.6--86.6% EM on synthetic evaluation but only 36.6--45.2% on HumanTime-500 for models with valid results on both splits, highlighting substantial limitations in generalization. We release the benchmark and code.

SHAKTI: Evidence-Grounded Conversational AI for Nutrition and Health
SHAKTI：面向营养与健康的基于证据的对话式人工智能
Chaitanya Pallerla, Dongyi Wang
cs.CL · cs.IR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) answer many diet and health questions but can state unsupported claims and cite sources that do not support them. We present SHAKTI (Smart Health Advisor for Knowledge-based Tailored Interventions), a conversational assistant that answers only from retrieved scholarly papers and exact food-composition data, and evaluate it with retrieval, generation, grounding, efficiency and contextawareness metrics. We indexed 484,368,086 OpenAlex works, searched exactly on a GPU for evaluation (10,065 NFCorpus, BioASQ, SciFact and PubMedQA questions) and through a compressed 230-million-abstract index in deployment. On 1,000 stratified questions, we compared single-shot, multi-hop, corrective and deep-research retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with Claude Sonnet. SHAKTI adds conversational query rewriting, USDA FoodData Central lookups, source-link checks and online verification of quotes and numbers. It was tested in 36 scripted conversational turns, a 248-question memory-depth test and a 38-question load test. Claims were checked by a Claude Opus judge against exactly the text the system saw. MedCPT reranking of hybrid retrieval gave the best MRR (0.21) and MAP@100 (0.14). Across existing RAG methods, faithfulness was 0.95-0.96, claim hallucination 0.5-0.8% and context precision up to 0.98; the deep-research agent answered 73.2% of BioASQ questions correctly. In conversation, SHAKTI reached a context-awareness score of 97.1%, faithfulness 95.5%, 1.9% unsupported claims, no contradicted claims and 229/229 working source links; it resolved references to the first question after 16 unrelated questions. An answer cost 14,716 tokens (US$0.06) with a median latency of 24 s. Large-scale retrieval with agentic evidence selection and mechanical verification yields auditable, low-hallucination nutrition answers.

cs.CL / 30 / 2611.30123
Parameter-Efficient Vocabulary Expansion via Cross-Lingual Embedding Alignment
通过跨语言嵌入对齐实现参数高效的词汇扩展
Andrew Ivan Soegeng, Muhammad Reza Qorib, Weishi Wang, Daniel Dahlmeier, Hwee Tou Ng
cs.CL · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Continual pretraining with vocabulary expansion is often used to make large language models (LLMs) more effective and efficient at handling new languages. However, when LLMs are extended to many languages simultaneously, the number of model parameters increases significantly. In addition, the newly added tokens do not receive the same number of training steps as the tokens in the original vocabulary, which sometimes causes vocabulary expansion to yield only limited performance improvements. We propose leveraging the semantic equivalence between words in the model's primary language and those in the extended vocabulary to transfer learned representations. In this paper, we introduce MATE, a parameter-efficient vocabulary expansion method that enables effective cross-lingual transfer with 8 times fewer additional parameters per token. MATE reduces the average tokenization compression ratio and delivers improvements on multiple benchmarks.

cs.CL / 31 / 2611.30141
Reading the Tea Leaves, Again: Can Large Language Models Predict Language Model Training Runs?
再次解读茶叶：大型语言模型能否预测语言模型的训练运行？
Xinran Zhao, Xiang Li, Tong Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Zichun Yu, Tongshuang Wu
cs.CL · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
LLM agents now propose research ideas and run the experiments that test them, but they train every run to its end, whereas a researcher reads a run's configuration and the beginning of its curve and stops the runs that show no promise. Reading a run this way takes more than describing or implementing a training method: it takes knowing what a design choice does to a run. We build Tea Leaves to measure this knowledge on 682 real training runs across pretraining, fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning (RL): a forecaster sees the first 20% of a run with its configuration, description, and code, and predicts the rest. Across 11 LLMs and a range of forecasting baselines, the strongest LLMs match or exceed the best curve fitter on smooth loss curves (skill 0.66 against 0.62) and lead on noisy RL reward curves (0.43 against 0.13). What bounds every forecaster is what the log carries: on sparsely logged community runs all methods lose most of their skill, and none reliably flags a failing run in advance. Beyond the curve, information helps and effort does not: related runs in the prompt cut the error on loss curves by 39%, and knowledge of training dynamics lets the strongest LLMs order all 36 pairs of runs that differ by a described code change, which the early curves do not separate, whereas tools add little. This knowledge can be learned from logged runs: a small open model trained on public runs matches the best LLM on loss curves. Applied to the progress curves of research agents, the same reading ranks tasks by their remaining headroom, although for a single agent run it does not improve on the last value. We release the benchmark, the trained readers, and their training data to test and train LLMs' understanding of training and to help research agents decide which runs deserve their compute.
Chinese Translation
LLM 智能体现在会提出研究想法，并运行检验这些想法的实验，但它们会把每一次运行都训练到结束，而研究者则会阅读一次运行的配置及其曲线的开头部分，并中止那些看不出前景的运行。以这种方式解读一次运行，所需要的不仅仅是描述或实现一种训练方法：还需要知道某个设计选择会对一次运行产生什么影响。我们构建了 Tea Leaves，在涵盖预训练、微调与强化学习（RL）的 682 次真实训练运行上测量这种知识：预测器会看到一次运行的前 20% 及其配置、描述和代码，并预测其余部分。在 11 个 LLM 和一系列预测基线上，最强的 LLM 在平滑的损失曲线上达到或超过最佳曲线拟合器（技能值 0.66 对 0.62），并在噪声较大的 RL 奖励曲线上领先（0.43 对 0.13）。限制每一个预测器的是日志所承载的信息：在日志稀疏的社区运行上，所有方法都失去了大部分技能值，而且没有任何方法能可靠地提前标记出一次失败的运行。在曲线之外，信息有帮助而投入的努力没有：在提示中加入相关运行可将损失曲线上的误差降低 39%，而对训练动力学的知识使最强的 LLM 能够对全部 36 对仅因某一所述代码改动而不同的运行进行排序，而这些运行仅靠早期曲线无法区分，相比之下工具的作用则微乎其微。这种知识可以从记录的运行中学习得到：一个在公开运行上训练的小型开放模型在损失曲线上与最佳 LLM 匹敌。应用于研究智能体的进展曲线时，同样的解读方式可以按剩余提升空间对任务进行排序，尽管对于单个智能体的运行而言，它相比最后一个取值并无改进。我们发布该基准、训练好的解读器及其训练数据，用以测试和训练 LLM 对训练的理解，并帮助研究智能体决定哪些运行值得投入它们的算力。

cs.CL / 32 / 2611.30168
FiRE: Fine-grained Ranking Evaluation for Machine Translation
FiRE：面向机器翻译的细粒度排序评估
Wenyang Gao, Yinghao Yang, Xi Jin, Jing Li, Yue Zhang
cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Developing reliable machine translation (MT) systems hinges on our ability to distinguish superior translations from inferior ones. However, existing evaluation paradigms, whether limited to coarse overall rankings or misaligned with human preferences, fail to deliver interpretable, fine-grained feedback in reference-free settings. We present a Fine-Grained Ranking Evaluation method (FiRE) that leverages off-the-shelf large language models to perform criterion-driven pairwise comparison across three complementary dimensions: faithfulness, fluency, and consistency of style, instead of producing a single holistic judgment. To enable rigorous meta-evaluation of evaluation paradigms in the absence of any suitable testbed, we construct the first human-annotated, reference-free benchmark for fine-grained ranking evaluation, achieving substantial inter-annotator agreement. Through meta-evaluation on this benchmark and existing MQM datasets, FiRE demonstrably outperforms regression-based and error-analysis metrics in aligning with human comparative judgments, while providing more informative insights into translation quality. Finally, our examination of LLM evaluator biases (position and self-enhancement) and their handling of tied cases offers guidance for more nuanced MT evaluation. Code and benchmark resources are available at https://github.com/wygao8/FiRE-MT.
Chinese Translation
开发可靠的机器翻译（MT）系统，取决于我们区分优质译文与劣质译文的能力。然而，现有的评估范式，无论是局限于粗粒度的整体排序，还是与人类偏好不一致，都无法在无参考（reference-free）环境下提供可解释的细粒度反馈。我们提出一种细粒度排序评估方法（FiRE），它利用现成的大型语言模型，在三个互补维度——忠实性、流畅性和风格一致性——上进行由准则驱动的成对比较，而不是给出单一的整体判断。为了在缺乏合适测试平台的情况下对评估范式进行严格的元评估，我们构建了首个用于细粒度排序评估的人工标注、无参考基准，并达到了高度（substantial）的标注者间一致性。通过在该基准和现有 MQM 数据集上的元评估，FiRE 在与人类比较判断的一致性方面明显优于基于回归的指标和错误分析指标，同时能提供关于翻译质量的更有信息量的洞见。最后，我们对 LLM 评估器偏差（位置偏差与自我增强偏差）及其对并列情况处理方式的考察，为更细致的机器翻译评估提供了指导。代码与基准资源见 https://github.com/wygao8/FiRE-MT。

cs.CL / 33 / 2611.30183
PCC: Pivotal Channel Compensation for Layer Pruning of Large Language Models
PCC：面向大语言模型层剪枝的关键通道补偿
Xiangqian Wang, Yucheng Zhang, Zhaohong Jia, Kun Jing, Chunchun Li
cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Treating independent layers as the minimal pruning unit allows layer pruning to efficiently eliminate many redundant parameters and achieve high compression rates. Layer pruning has become a promising and prevalent structured pruning technique for large language models (LLMs). However, multi-layer removal can lead to significant performance degradation for LLMs. Although some works have explored various compensation methods for pruned layers, they are inefficient and costly. Observing that the expression of a large proportion of information is concentrated on a small number of pivotal channels, we propose a novel post-pruning compensation method for layer pruning, called pivotal channel compensation (PCC). PCC can achieve significant performance improvement by compensating for a small number of channels through learnable linear transformations at the pruning interface. Besides, we propose a new evaluation metric, called channel-wise average performance improvement (CAPI), which can measure the efficiency of channel-wise compensation. Our experimental results across various LLMs demonstrate that PCC can achieve significant and consistent improvements and high CAPI on language modeling and zero-shot question answering for the state-of-the-art cross-layer and consecutive-layer pruning methods. Compared with existing compensation methods, PCC can achieve competitive results with fewer additional parameters and less training cost.
Chinese Translation
将独立层视为最小剪枝单元，使得层剪枝能够高效地消除大量冗余参数并获得高压缩率。层剪枝已成为大语言模型（LLMs）中一种有前景且普遍采用的结构化剪枝技术。然而，多层移除会导致 LLMs 性能显著下降。尽管一些工作已经探索了针对被剪枝层的各种补偿方法，但它们效率低下且成本高昂。观察到很大比例的信息表达集中于少数关键通道上，我们提出了一种新颖的面向层剪枝的剪枝后补偿方法，称为关键通道补偿（PCC）。PCC 通过在剪枝接口处通过可学习的线性变换对少量通道进行补偿，能够实现显著的性能提升。此外，我们提出了一种新的评估指标，称为通道级平均性能提升（CAPI），它可以衡量通道级补偿的效率。我们在多种 LLMs 上的实验结果表明，对于最先进的跨层剪枝和连续层剪枝方法，PCC 在语言建模和零样本问答上能够取得显著且一致的提升以及高 CAPI。与现有补偿方法相比，PCC 能够以更少的额外参数和更低的训练成本取得有竞争力的结果。

cs.CL / 34 / 2611.30196
Laya-IsoToken: Day-One Clinical Codebook Switching via Closed-Form Operator Compilation
Laya-IsoToken：通过闭式算子编译实现首日临床代码本切换
Zeqiang Wang
cs.CL · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Healthcare systems periodically revise diagnostic and procedural classifications (ICD-9 to ICD-10/11), update hospital reimbursement groupers (MS-DRG), and deploy clinical coding across languages. Supervised coding networks bind clinical text encoders to fixed per-code classifier weights, forcing hospitals to re-annotate tens of thousands of records before switching codebooks, whereas standalone large language models incur high latency and hallucinate invalid codes. Here we show that day-one clinical codebook switching becomes feasible without target-labeled notes when local clinical evidence reading is decoupled from a strictly frozen multilingual concept space. Laya-IsoToken trains a clinical span reader once on source records with zero per-code classifier parameters, separating text evidence from historical disease prevalence. Given only public target code descriptions, closed-form matrix compilation aligns distributional shifts, compensates for paraphrased definitions, and deduplicates sibling codes in under three seconds, while a pre-deployment geometric residual routes unfamiliar concepts to offline language model verification. Across 32,804 MIMIC-IV ICD-9 discharges, Laya-IsoToken matches published supervised baselines (62.6% Micro-F1) while reducing active calibration error by 32%. Switched with zero target training notes to 13,783 unseen-patient ICD-10 discharges, MS-DRG groups, and multilingual cohorts, it outperforms biomedical dense retrievers, semantic crosswalks (+5.4 F1 points on ICD-10, paired $d_z = 0.49$, $p < 0.001$), and official US CMS equivalence mappings (+3.5 points, $p < 0.001$) at 9.4 ms per admission. Pairing this reader with an offline 31B verifier across 1,000 full discharge summaries lifts zero-training ICD-10 coding to 40.6% Micro-F1 (57.0% category F1, $d_z = 0.66$, $p < 0.001$) with 0.0% invalid code hallucinations.
Chinese Translation
医疗系统会定期修订诊断与操作分类（ICD-9 到 ICD-10/11），更新医院报销分组器（MS-DRG），并跨语言部署临床编码。有监督编码网络将临床文本编码器绑定到固定的逐代码分类器权重上，迫使医院在切换代码本之前重新标注数万条记录，而独立的大语言模型则具有高延迟并会幻觉出无效代码。在此我们表明，当局部临床证据读取与严格冻结的多语言概念空间解耦时，无需目标标注病历即可实现首日临床代码本切换。Laya-IsoToken 在源记录上一次性训练一个临床片段读取器，且具有零逐代码分类器参数，从而将文本证据与历史疾病患病率分离。仅给定公开的目标代码描述，闭式矩阵编译即可对齐分布偏移、补偿被改写的定义，并在三秒内对同级代码去重，而部署前的几何残差会将不熟悉的概念路由至离线语言模型验证。在 32,804 例 MIMIC-IV ICD-9 出院记录上，Laya-IsoToken 与已发表的有监督基线（62.6% Micro-F1）相当，同时将主动校准误差降低 32%。在零目标训练病历条件下切换至 13,783 例未见患者 ICD-10 出院记录、MS-DRG 分组和多语言队列时，它以每次入院 9.4 ms 的速度优于生物医学稠密检索器、语义交叉映射（在 ICD-10 上 +5.4 F1 点，配对 $d_z = 0.49$，$p < 0.001$）以及美国 CMS 官方等价映射（+3.5 点，$p < 0.001$）。将该读取器与离线 31B 验证器配对，在 1,000 份完整出院小结上，将零训练 ICD-10 编码提升至 40.6% Micro-F1（57.0% 类别 F1，$d_z = 0.66$，$p < 0.001$），且无效代码幻觉为 0.0%。

cs.CL / 35 / 2611.30218
Ontology-Compiled 2D Clinical State Fields with Bidirectional Diffusion Encoders for Zero-Training Cross-Ontology Medical Coding
用于零训练跨本体医学编码的、采用双向扩散编码器的本体编译二维临床状态场
Zeqiang Wang
cs.CL · cs.IR · cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Healthcare systems continually revise clinical taxonomies, update reimbursement schedules, and harmonize cross-border registries. Existing automated coding models bind clinical text understanding to fixed vocabulary-specific heads, requiring manual relabeling and retraining whenever code sets change. We introduce Ontology-Compiled 2D Clinical State Fields (OCSF), a vocabulary-free framework that decouples clinical document reading from target ontology indexing so one trained encoder can switch across arbitrary medical vocabularies in seconds without target training. A single-pass bidirectional diffusion-pretrained encoder and vocabulary-free decoder map each clinical note into a fixed-dimension two-dimensional state matrix with zero code-specific parameters. Any target ontology is compiled offline on CPU from public text descriptions into a scale-invariant Tikhonov deconvolution operator that suppresses sibling-code interference while preserving source decision thresholds. Trained solely on English MIMIC-IV ICD-9 discharge summaries and evaluated without target tuning across 58,706 held-out test notes and five unseen ontologies spanning English ICD-10, MS-DRG, Spanish, Greek, and Chinese (115-185,458 codes), OCSF reaches 63.15% Micro-F1 on in-domain ICD-9 (outperforming a matched closed-vocabulary classifier and eliminating late-epoch tail overfitting) and transfers directly to 26,085 English ICD-10 codes (29.23% recall at gold cardinality), MS-DRG groups, and multilingual terminologies, compiling up to 185,458 codes in under 10 seconds on CPU with sub-millisecond GPU readout.
Chinese Translation
医疗系统不断修订临床分类法、更新报销目录，并协调跨境登记库。现有的自动编码模型将临床文本理解绑定到固定的、特定词表的输出头，每当代码集变化时都需要手动重新标注和重新训练。我们提出本体编译二维临床状态场（OCSF），这是一个无词表框架，将临床文档读取与目标本体索引解耦，使一个训练好的编码器无需目标训练即可在数秒内切换至任意医学词表。一个单遍双向扩散预训练编码器与无词表解码器将每份临床记录映射为固定维度的二维状态矩阵，且零代码特定参数。任何目标本体均在CPU上离线地从公开文本描述编译为尺度不变的Tikhonov反卷积算子，该算子抑制兄弟代码干扰，同时保留源决策阈值。OCSF仅使用英语MIMIC-IV ICD-9出院小结训练，并在不进行目标调优的情况下跨58,706份留出测试记录和五个未见本体进行评估，这些本体涵盖英语ICD-10、MS-DRG、西班牙语、希腊语和中文（115-185,458个代码），其在域内ICD-9上达到63.15%的Micro-F1（优于匹配的封闭词表分类器，并消除后期轮次尾部过拟合），并直接迁移至26,085个英语ICD-10代码（金标准基数下召回率为29.23%）、MS-DRG分组和多语言术语体系，在CPU上不到10秒编译多达185,458个代码，并具有亚毫秒级GPU读出。

cs.CL / 36 / 2611.30406
TAP: Policy Interfaces for Diffusion Language Models
TAP：扩散语言模型的策略接口
Preeti, Ankita Kushwaha, Kiran Ravish, Pawan Kumar
cs.CL · cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion language models denoise a masked canvas, making them a natural setting for selective generation decisions such as answering, waiting, clarifying, or refusing. We introduce TAP-DiLM, which adds a typed policy variable to masked diffusion LMs, and study how this policy should be attached to the denoising process. Across BERT-base, MDLMOWT, LLaDA-8B, and Dream-7B, we compare shared-vocabulary slots, dedicated slot heads, and CLS-based external heads. The results reveal a clear interface-backbone interaction: dedicated heads provide robust policy learning across scales, while sharedvocabulary heads can be effective when the LM-head geometry is favorable. A simple LMhead sharpness probe predicts when sharedhead policy internalization is reliable, giving a practical diagnostic for interface selection. Causal clamp and slot-injection tests show that dedicated policy slots can influence body denoising through feedback, especially at 8B scale. Safety-refusal experiments further show that TAP-DiLM supports competitive typed refusal behavior when trained with diverse unsafe prompts.
Chinese Translation
扩散语言模型对掩码画布进行去噪，这使其成为进行选择性生成决策（如回答、等待、澄清或拒绝）的自然场景。我们引入 TAP-DiLM，它向掩码扩散语言模型添加一个类型化策略变量，并研究该策略应如何附加到去噪过程中。在 BERT-base、MDLMOWT、LLaDA-8B 和 Dream-7B 上，我们比较了共享词汇槽、专用槽头和基于 CLS 的外部头。结果揭示了明显的接口-骨干交互：专用头跨规模提供稳健的策略学习，而共享词汇头在 LM 头几何有利时可以有效。一个简单的 LM 头锐度探针可预测共享头策略内化何时可靠，为接口选择提供实用诊断。因果钳制和槽注入测试表明，专用策略槽可以通过反馈影响主体去噪，尤其是在 8B 规模下。安全拒绝实验进一步表明，当使用多样化不安全提示进行训练时，TAP-DiLM 支持具有竞争力的类型化拒绝行为。

cs.CL / 37 / 2611.30460
Rethinking the Evaluation of Contrastive Decoding for Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Large Language Models
重新思考多模态大语言模型中幻觉缓解的对比解码评估
Ting Chen, Geng Li, Guohao Chen, Hanjia Lyu
cs.CL · cs.CV
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Contrastive decoding (CD) mitigates object hallucination in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by contrasting token distributions under different conditions to adjust token scores. However, existing generative and discriminative benchmarks primarily measure final task scores, which can be confounded by candidate filtering, changes in generation trajectories, and response biases, making it difficult to isolate the effects of the underlying contrastive adjustments. To address these limitations while complementing existing evaluations, we introduce CONCOR (Contrastive Correction Evaluation), a controlled benchmark that directly evaluates the competition between ground-truth and different types of hallucinated candidates using the Contrastive Grounding Margin (CGM). CGM also enables analysis of directional consistency, composition, and reliability of contrastive corrections. Our evaluation reveals that existing CD methods exhibit distinct correction behaviors: some consistently favor ground-truth candidates, whereas others produce strong corrections but also introduce more errors. Crucially, these differences help explain their contrasting responses to increased contrast strength, which improves some methods while degrading others. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating the contrastive correction itself, rather than relying solely on final-output performance, and CONCOR provides a controlled and interpretable framework for understanding and improving CD methods for hallucination mitigation.
Chinese Translation
对比解码（CD）通过对比不同条件下的 token 分布来调整 token 分数，从而缓解多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）中的物体幻觉。然而，现有的生成式和判别式基准主要衡量最终任务分数，这些分数可能受到候选过滤、生成轨迹变化和响应偏差的混淆，因而难以分离底层对比调整所带来的影响。为在补充现有评估的同时解决这些局限，我们引入 CONCOR（Contrastive Correction Evaluation，对比校正评估），这是一个受控基准，使用对比接地裕度（Contrastive Grounding Margin, CGM）直接评估真实答案候选与不同类型幻觉候选之间的竞争。CGM 还使得能够分析对比校正的方向一致性、组成和可靠性。我们的评估揭示，现有 CD 方法表现出不同的校正行为：一些方法始终偏向真实答案候选，而另一些方法产生强校正但也引入更多错误。关键的是，这些差异有助于解释它们对对比强度增加的不同响应：对比强度增加会改善某些方法，却会降低另一些方法的性能。这些发现凸显了评估对比校正本身的重要性，而不是仅依赖最终输出性能；CONCOR 为理解和改进用于缓解幻觉的 CD 方法提供了一个受控且可解释的框架。

cs.CL / 38 / 2611.30587
Quantizing Diffusion LLMs under Parallel Decoding: Commitment Risk and the Parallelism Tax
并行解码下扩散大语言模型的量化：承诺风险与并行税
Huan Xu, Maosen Zhao, Pengtao Chen, Tao Chen
cs.CL
diffusionlarge language model
扩散模型相关
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) are served with accelerated decoders that cache context and commit, in one step, every masked position whose confidence clears a threshold. Yet post-training quantization of dLLMs has so far been calibrated and evaluated under fixed-step samplers without caching. We study W4A4 quantization under the deployed decoder and find that the decoder determines both where quantization harms accuracy and what it costs. Irreversible errors enter chiefly through forced commitments, made when no position clears the threshold: they are a minority of commitments but carry most quantization-induced flips. Quantization also levies a parallelism tax, extra forward passes per response: by compressing top logit gaps, it pushes positions below the threshold while leaving predictions largely intact. We propose DECAL, which reweights layer-wise calibration by a commitment-risk prior measured on the deployed decoder, and an argmax-preserving commit temperature that recovers the tax. On LLaDA and Dream, DECAL attains the best average accuracy among W4A4 methods, with lower run-to-run variance than the closest existing calibration method.
Chinese Translation
扩散大语言模型（dLLMs）在服务时采用加速解码器，这些解码器会缓存上下文，并在一步中提交所有置信度超过阈值的掩码位置。然而，迄今为止，dLLMs 的训后量化都是在不带缓存的固定步采样器下进行校准和评估的。我们研究了部署解码器下的 W4A4 量化，发现解码器既决定了量化在何处损害准确率，也决定了其代价。不可逆误差主要通过强制承诺进入，即在没有任何位置超过阈值时所做的提交：它们只占承诺的少数，却承载了大多数由量化引起的翻转。量化还会征收一种并行税，即每个响应额外的前向传播：通过压缩 top logit 差距，它把位置推到阈值以下，同时使预测基本保持不变。我们提出 DECAL，它通过在部署解码器上测得的承诺风险先验对逐层校准进行重加权，并采用一种保持 argmax 的提交温度来回收该税。在 LLaDA 和 Dream 上，DECAL 在 W4A4 方法中取得了最佳平均准确率，且运行间方差低于最接近的现有校准方法。

From Rewarding What Models Say to How They Think: Attention Process Reward Model for LLM Reinforcement Learning
从奖励模型“说什么”到“如何思考”：面向LLM强化学习的注意力过程奖励模型
Kairong Han, Nuanqiao Shan, Ziyu Zhao, Xinpeng Dong, Zijing Hu, Dian Jin, Leyan Deng, Junjian Ye, Lujia Pan, Fei Wu, Kun Kuang
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Reinforcement learning (RL) has become an important component in large language models (LLMs). However, existing RL approaches focus on final outputs or textual solution trajectories, leading to coarse-grained rewards and unreliable reasoning. Such paradigms focus mainly on what the model outputs while overlooking how the model internally reasons. Therefore, can we reward how a model thinks internally rather than merely what it says? We first reveal the problem of textual reward aliasing in existing reward modeling approaches. Motivated by this, we propose the Attention Process Reward Model (APRM), which assigns internal rewards based on hidden states and attention maps to capture high-quality reasoning patterns. With only approximately 46M parameters, APRM is trained using ranking and counterfactual objectives, and its reward guides RL optimization while being periodically updated to handle distribution shifts. Integrated with representative RL methods, APRM achieved an average pass@8 gain of 2.88\%. Our results demonstrate the promise of incorporating internal reasoning signals into RL for LLMs.

Abstract
Trallie is an open-source framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to perform information extraction (IE) from natural language sources with or without user guidance. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on extensive labeled datasets or domain-specific training, Trallie enables the conversion of unstructured data into structured formats with minimal or no representative examples. The framework is designed with three key objectives: (i) reducing manual annotation by harnessing prompt-based zero-shot and few-shot capabilities of modern LLMs, (ii) flexibly parsing diverse document formats (i.e., HTML, PDF, TXT, and JSON), and (iii) improving accessibility for non-expert users by automatically inducing schemas from document collections, which can then be refined for extraction. We evaluate Trallie with open-weight LLMs on FDA 510(k) documents and on movie and university websites from SWDE. It outperforms previously reported systems when the target attributes are provided for text extraction and is competitive when it must discover attributes for the schema automatically. The project is available at https://github.com/PiSchool/trallie

Abstract
Auditing corporate sustainability reports requires assurance professionals to map a company-specific checklist drawn from roughly 1,700 regulatory requirements onto the relevant passages of lengthy, repeatedly revised draft reports and to judge compliance. We present SARA (Sustainability Reporting Assistant), a human-in-the-loop recommender system delivered as a Microsoft Word add-in that recommends, for each requirement, the passages addressing it and predicts a compliance verdict while keeping the auditor in full control. SARA casts auditing as content-based recommendation over a fixed regulatory taxonomy and makes per-requirement large language model (LLM) matching cheaper, faster, and more accurate through topic-prediction filtering: on expert-annotated reports, it reduces matching cost about sixfold and runtime by 42% versus feeding the full report to the LLM. It is in production use across PwC Germany's sustainability-assurance practice.
