Semantic-aware Decoding for Diverse Text-to-SQL under Schema Ambiguity
面向模式歧义下多样化文本到SQL的语义感知解码
Yuxuan Jiang, Anna Mitsopoulou, Apostolos Koukouvinis, Yannis Velegrakis, Georgia Koutrika
cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Real-world text-to-SQL systems often face schema ambiguity, where a question can map to multiple plausible schema elements. To support downstream disambiguation, SQL generation systems should include diverse interpretations among their top-k predictions. However, large language models (LLMs) typically favor a single interpretation, producing highly skewed outputs. We propose Semantic-aware Logit Adjustment (SLA), a training-free decoding method that promotes diverse SQL generation by adjusting token logits based on semantic similarity between schema elements. Unlike prior approaches that rely on reasoning-intensive prompting or task-specific fine-tuning, SLA is efficient, model-agnostic, and easy to deploy. Experiments show that SLA consistently improves interpretation coverage over standard decoding and remains competitive with existing diversity-oriented methods at substantially lower inference cost.

PRIMEAPE：用于评判模型细粒度元评估的多语言基准
Vladislav Mikhailov, Sarfraz Ahmad, Momina Ahsan, Zoia Butenko, Vladimir Dobrovolskii, Preslav Nakov, Erik Velldal, Lilja Øvrelid, Ekaterina Artemova
cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models increasingly serve as judges of other models, shaping benchmark rankings and model development. Yet, a judge whose rationale consistently supports its verdict may still disagree with human preferences. To study this, we introduce PRIMEAPE, a multilingual benchmark for evaluating judge verdicts and rationales. PRIMEAPE provides 2,205 response pairs covering 243 instructions in English, French, Spanish, Urdu, Hindi, Norwegian Bokmål, and Yoruba, with 11k human annotations of preferences and rationales across relevance, naturalness, truthfulness, safety, and overall quality. Our evaluation of twelve open- and closed-weight judges reveals that aggregate performance conceals differences across languages and criteria, while requesting rationales does not consistently improve agreement with human preferences. Judges also favor the first position, longer responses, and responses from related models, with effects that vary across criteria and languages. Crucially, judges can justify verdicts that disagree with human preferences while maintaining consistency between their verdicts and rationales. These findings show that consistency with a judge's own verdict does not establish alignment with human judgment. PRIMEAPE enables assessment of both, providing a foundation for more reliable multilingual judges. We release our benchmark and all annotation materials under the CC BY-NC 4.0 license at github.com/Toloka/primeape.

Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time
超越自一致性：测试时的递归自我改进
Jianyu Wu, Yizhou Wang, Encheng Su, Jinouwen Zhang, Pengze Li, Lintao Wang, Chen Tang, Aoran Wang, Wanli Ouyang, Shixiang Tang
cs.CL · cs.AI · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) that continue improving after deployment (e.g., recursive self-improvement) offer a promising path toward general intelligence. Current test-time methods pursue this goal on unlabeled questions, primarily relying on self-consistency: they generate independent solutions and use majority voting to select an answer or construct training targets. This leaves earlier reasoning unused at inference and can reinforce an incorrect majority during training. Humans instead build on earlier attempts to preserve useful reasoning, correct mistakes and improve their problem-solving strategies. Following this principle, we propose Test-Time Recursive Self-Improvement (TT-RSI), a label-free framework for improving LLMs at test time through two mutually reinforcing components: (1) In-Context RSI repeatedly re-solves each question using the full previous solution as a reference, letting the model decide whether and how to use it so that inference compute builds on earlier reasoning. (2) In-Weight RSI distills successive refinements into the model's weights, enabling progress beyond an initially wrong majority and theoretically bringing the first attempt toward the model's infinite-step refinement limit. The updated model answers better and refines more effectively, generating stronger references for subsequent training. Extensive experiments show that TT-RSI improves average accuracy by +13.89% over the base model and outperforms the strongest self-consistency-based method by +4.79% under the same test-time scaling budget.

大语言模型（LLMs）在部署后仍能持续改进（例如递归自我改进），为通往通用智能提供了一条有前景的路径。当前的测试时方法在无标签问题上追求这一目标，主要依赖自一致性：它们生成独立的解答，并使用多数投票来选择答案或构建训练目标。这使得先前的推理在推理阶段未被利用，并可能在训练期间强化错误的多数。人类则基于先前的尝试来保留有用的推理、纠正错误并改进其问题解决策略。遵循这一原则，我们提出测试时递归自我改进（TT-RSI），一个无标签框架，通过两个相互增强的组件在测试时改进 LLMs：（1）上下文内 RSI 反复重新求解每个问题，使用完整的先前解答作为参考，让模型决定是否以及如何使用它，从而使推理计算建立在先前推理之上。（2）权重内 RSI 将连续的细化蒸馏到模型权重中，使进展能够超越最初错误的多数，并在理论上将首次尝试推向模型的无限步细化极限。更新后的模型回答得更好，也更有效地进行细化，为后续训练生成更强的参考。大量实验表明，TT-RSI 相比基础模型将平均准确率提高了 +13.89%，并在相同的测试时扩展预算下以 +4.79% 的优势优于最强的基于自一致性的方法。

LODESTONE: Linking System Events to Threat Intelligence for Evidence-Grounded Cyber Attack Investigation
LODESTONE：将系统事件与威胁情报关联以实现基于证据的网络攻击调查

cs.CR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
System provenance graphs help reconstruct attacks through causal dependencies, but these connections alone do not explain how events accomplish an adversary's goal. Cyber threat intelligence (CTI) provides the necessary security knowledge, yet linking it to execution evidence requires bridging differences in meaning and granularity between events and attack relations amid scarce labels and sparse relevant evidence. We present LODESTONE, a cross-graph alignment system that links observed system events to CTI attack relations to support evidence-grounded attack reports. LODESTONE uses a novel CTI-driven training-data engine and an expert-verified benchmark of edge-level correspondences and reference attack reports. The engine pairs real CTI knowledge graphs with provenance graphs from isolated executions. A large language model (LLM) agent recursively improves correspondences by checking execution evidence and repairing retrieval, parsing, and reproduction failures; experts independently verify benchmark correspondences. LODESTONE combines text cross-encoder and directed-graph relevance scores to extract compact alert-centered subgraphs, retrieves article-level knowledge graphs through node- and edge-level dual-softmax assignment, and uses a fine-tuned 4B-parameter LLM to align event combinations with CTI attack steps. We evaluate LODESTONE on 27 expert-verified attack cases amid continuous benign activity from real applications, using 713 CTI articles. LLM judgments aligned with multiple human experts yield an attack-step description score of 82%, and attack identification reaches 91%, versus 73% and 32% using the same generator with provenance alone. Baseline pipelines and coding agents achieve description scores of at most 57%. Human-verified correspondences further demonstrate advantages in balancing attack-edge coverage with subgraph size, CTI retrieval, and cross-graph alignment.

CHIP：对比式硬件-图像投影。OpenAI CLIP 能否从 CPU 计算足迹重建图像？

Abstract
Image inference on a shared CPU leaves input-dependent traces in software-visible performance counters and execution time. CHIP (Contrastive Hardware-Image Projection) trains a lightweight residual projector on public images to map these measurements into the 768-dimensional visual embedding space of a frozen OpenAI CLIP model. A frozen Stable unCLIP generator uses the projected embeddings to reconstruct recognizable color scenes for held-out inputs. The attack requires no physical probe, candidate image gallery, domain-specific generator, or shared cache, and elapsed time alone retains the signal. We evaluate full-counter, single-counter, and timing-only measurements on Intel Haswell and Sapphire Rapids. The projected embeddings achieve 0.85 ROC AUC for held-out image identification, compared with a 0.50 baseline. Exact-image top-five retrieval reaches 24% on CIFAR-100 and 56% on Unsafe-Diffusion. cs.CR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model agents increasingly use third-party tools to complete user tasks. Even without malicious intent, they may fill broad or weakly constrained fields with private information that is unnecessary or inappropriate for the receiving tool. Such calls can satisfy the tool schema and complete the task, yet still violate minimum-necessary disclosure. We introduce ArguShield, a mediation layer that intercepts proposed tool calls before execution. It evaluates each candidate value using three signals: Value Provenance, Task Relevance, and Disclosure Boundary. ArguShield releases justified values, defers values that need user confirmation, and withholds those outside the permitted scope. We evaluate ArguShield with four tool-calling models on ArgPrivBench, a benchmark of 120 tasks across Travel, Shopping, and Healthcare. Unprotected agents frequently over-disclose private information despite high task success. Prompt-only protection reduces unauthorized disclosure but substantially lowers task success. ArguShield reduces unauthorized silent release to 9% on Standard tasks and 6% on High-risk tasks while preserving recoverable task success under simulated user confirmation.

Bounded Autonomy: A Trust-Anchored Defense Against Resource-Exhaustion Attacks on Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
有界自主性：一种抵御工具增强型 LLM 智能体资源耗尽攻击的信任锚定防御
Ziyuan Chen, Yueming Lyu, Songze Li, Huafeng Chen, Caifeng Shan
cs.CR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Tool-augmented Large Language Model (LLM) agents are vulnerable to resource-exhaustion attacks that amplify model-token consumption through persistent context amplification, large tool output amplification, and error-induced agentic loops. Despite growing attention to agent security and resource-abuse risks, a systematic defense framework specifically targeting these attacks remains lacking. Meanwhile, existing general-purpose agent defense frameworks, which address a broader range of security threats, often rely on prompt-level safeguards or coarse-grained resource limits and lack deterministic runtime mechanisms for controlling token consumption. They also provide limited support for balancing fault recovery against the risk of repeated resource-consuming execution. To address these limitations, we propose a trust-anchored closed-loop defense framework consisting of four phases: certificate-guided orchestration with deterministic handoffs, calibrated one-time node budgeting, Gateway-based runtime enforcement, and bounded recovery through a shared, non-resettable recovery pool. By accounting for both input and output tokens across all model invocations, our experiments demonstrate that the framework bounds cumulative token consumption, mitigates resource-amplification attacks, and preserves benign task utility under trusted execution assumptions.

POMA: Beyond Final Flags -- Process-Level Evaluation of Base LLMs in Vulnerability Exploitation

cs.CR · cs.SE
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
As large language models (LLMs) evolve from text generation to autonomous software-engineering execution, automated vulnerability exploitability verification has emerged as a vital frontier in software quality assurance and security validation. Existing security benchmarks, however, largely judge models by binary pass/fail outcomes or coarse stage milestones. Such outcome-centric scoring obscures fine-grained failure dynamics across long-horizon execution and conflates the intrinsic capability of a base LLM with external agent scaffolding. We present POMA (Pwn-Oriented Model Assessment), a process-level evaluation methodology and platform that isolates base LLMs under a unified execution baseline -- fixing task inputs, tool interfaces, target environments, feedback formats, and execution budgets -- while measuring intermediate states and transitions from runtime evidence. Evaluating four frontier base LLMs across 55 CTF Pwn challenges and 10 real-world vulnerability reproduction tasks exposes persistent capability attrition along the exploitation chain: from vulnerability knowledge to executable implementation, from client-side actions to verified target states, from failure localization to precise repair, and across iterative revisions. In real-world software, models further struggle to satisfy format, semantic, differential, and crash-identity constraints simultaneously. By pinpointing where execution chains break down, POMA provides an empirical foundation for trustworthy capability assessment and principled vulnerability-agent design. Our benchmark catalogs, process-measurement evaluator, and sample harness are publicly available at https://github.com/maple-pwn/poma-release .

Carried-Over and Agent-Native Threats in the Supply Chain of LLM Agent Skills
LLM 智能体技能供应链中的继承性威胁与智能体原生威胁
Kaixuan Li, Wenbo Guo, Sen Chen, Yang Liu
cs.CR · cs.SE
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Agent skills are reusable packages that extend a large language model (LLM) agent with scripts, third-party dependencies, and natural-language instructions. An agent builds a skill's arguments from user requests and untrusted external content, so a flaw left by a benign author can escalate a prompt injection to code execution. Existing studies target malicious skills or a single attack vector, and none tests whether an agent can reach such flaws. We present the first registry-scale empirical study of the supply chain attack surface arising from unintentional vulnerabilities in agent skills, over all 48,682 skills in ClawHub. The study covers two carried-over risks, dependencies and first-party code, and two agent-native ones, install instructions and credentials printed to stdout. We screen all skills by static analysis, manually review all 3,428 cases flagged by the four main detectors, and test reachability by running sampled flagged skills in a sandbox and with a live LLM agent under indirect prompt injection. First, dependency risk carries over in a different form: 49.6% of the skills with resolvable dependencies depend on a version with a known CVE, and unlike npm packages, which mostly become vulnerable after release, 78.3% of them are born vulnerable, already exposed at publication. Second, few of these CVEs are reachable: agent input reaches the vulnerable function in only 3.0% of the affected skills, whereas 21 of 22 sampled first-party flaws are exploited end to end in the sandbox. Third, a live agent executes the injected payload in 48.5% of the sampled flagged skills, but almost always in its own shell before the skill runs, and the payload reaches a flaw in the skill itself in only 5.0%. Hence, registries should prioritize first-party flaws over dependency alerts, and agent runtimes should not pass skill arguments through a shell.

S1Arena-MM: Which Multimodal Decisions Can Be Left to System 1?

Lang Lin, Tianyu Chen, Yi Gu, Yang Zhao, Xinran Song, Xinyang Liu, Jianpeng Cheng, Mingyuan Zhou
cs.CV · cs.AI · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Perception systems often make discrete decisions: flag a hateful meme, predict whether a pedestrian will cross, detect a spoofed voice, or select the next move in a game. System-1 models, such as OneJev and Jev-Omni, read the media and return probabilities over the options in a single forward pass, while multimodal large language models (MLLMs) generate text. Which multimodal decisions can System-1 models handle, and where do MLLMs perform better? We introduce S1Arena-MM, a benchmark that gives every model the same decision requests and scores the probabilities it returns. It contains 51,060 questions across 94 tasks with image, video, and audio input, drawn from 94 public datasets and three program-generated ones. It also includes 102 closed-loop game environments that a model plays from screenshots; in real-time mode, the game continues while the model decides. We evaluate 33 open models: 12 System-1 models and 21 MLLMs read at the answer token. On static decisions, the best System-1 model leads the best MLLM by 4.9 percentage points on images and is within one point of it on video and audio. Post-training for decisions mainly improves the probabilities: on video, a System-1 model has a lower Brier score than the MLLM that it is post-trained from in 10 of 12 pairs. With up to 2,048 thought tokens per question, the most accurate MLLMs pass the best System-1 models only slightly, and thinking raises the Brier score of most MLLMs. Closed loops separate the models: three System-1 models built on a 27B MLLM reach 22.0-33.3% progression in BALROG, and no other model exceeds 9.7% with thinking off. In real-time GameWorld, latencies of up to 1.1 s per decision cause no measurable loss of progress for System-1 models. Code and data: https://github.com/zhaoyang02/S1Arena-MM.

Audio-Visual Rearrangement
视听重排列
Ruohao Guo, Jiatong Ye, Chenwei Dong, Jinxing Zhou, Dantong Niu, Guangyao Li, Zhenbo Li
cs.CV · cs.AI · cs.MM · cs.SD
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
We introduce Audio-Visual Rearrangement (AVR), a novel task in which an agent hears a spoken request, retrieves a suitable object, and delivers it to the requesting user or an instruction-specified destination. AVR requires the agent to understand the spoken request and acoustically localize the speaker for delivery. To support this task, we construct a dataset covering three query types: explicit target specification, speaker-relative spatial references, and implicit user intent, spanning eight subtypes with diverse object selection and delivery requirements. Moreover, we propose a framework that integrates a motion-aware spatial audio module into an audio-visual large language model to encode spatial cues from the spoken request and update them as the agent moves. We further incorporate auxiliary supervision for speech understanding, spatial audio perception, and visual grounding through multitask instruction tuning to improve action prediction. Experiments establish baseline performance in both seen and unseen environments, laying the groundwork for future research on embodied intelligence and human-robot interaction. The code will be publicly available soon.

TriSegAgent: Context-Efficient 3D Annotation with MLLMs via Tri-Planes
TriSegAgent：通过三平面利用 MLLM 实现上下文高效的三维标注
Qingqiao Hu, Jialin Li, Meilong Xu, Kehan Qi, Yipeng Zhang, Lin Tian, Hongwei Bran Li, Klaus Mueller, Xiaoling Hu
cs.CV · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Interactive segmentation models turn a few clicks into a segmentation prediction across domains, so annotators only decide where the prediction still needs correction. Annotation thus becomes a loop of inspecting the prediction and clicking again. Each step of this loop is a visual judgment, which suits general-purpose multimodal large language model (MLLM) agents. In this work, we focus on letting these agents run this loop on 3D volumes. However, the MLLM in such an agent takes only 2D images as input, so the agent must observe the 3D volume in 2D. Since the loop calls the MLLM many times, this observation must be token-compact enough to keep every call cheap, yet informative enough to show error regions in the 3D prediction. We meet both needs with tri-planes, the three orthogonal planes that cross at one point in the volume. We show, both theoretically and empirically, that tri-planes are context-efficient yet keep sufficient detail to show error regions in the 3D prediction. Building on tri-planes, we introduce TriSegAgent, an MLLM agent that refines the 3D prediction iteratively. Within the agent, the MLLM only judges the prediction on tri-planes, while a visual harness turns each judgment into a 3D action in code. To make the loop reliable, the harness places each click at an exact voxel in the volume and checks whether to accept the 3D prediction. To evaluate the agent, we build a diverse benchmark of 690 regions of interest (ROIs) from 35 public medical datasets across three imaging modalities. With frontier MLLMs, TriSegAgent reaches an overall Dice about 10 points above the strongest baseline, and its lead is even larger on targets below 3 cm. With flash-level MLLMs, it outperforms a recent 3D segmentation agent built on a frontier MLLM.

cs.CV · cs.LG

Abstract
Diffusion virtual try-on (VTO) models produce convincing garment transfers from a single product photograph, but at hundreds of milliseconds to seconds per image every deployment today is offline or falls back to AR mirrors that need a rigged 3D asset per product. We present LiveMirror, a live-camera try-on mirror that renders a flat garment photograph onto a moving person with a diffusion model on one 16 GB consumer GPU. Its core is asynchronous keyframe try-on: generation never blocks the display, every displayed frame is an optical-flow warp of the latest generated keyframe, and keyframes are replaced only through a cross-fade. The display runs at camera rate (25 FPS at 720p) while a new try-on arrives every 370-490 ms; we measure the residual flicker, give a stage-by-stage latency budget, and report which accelerations (step count, consistency LoRA, tiny decoder, compilation) keep garment prints intact. We then show that the same GPU fixes the model's biggest cultural blind spot: try-on models trained on VITON-HD and DressCode render a knee-length kurta or sherwani as a torso-length top or a dress over bare legs. A thigh-covering mask, self-supervised pairs built automatically from 24.9k on-model e-commerce photographs, and 3.2 GPU-hours of attention-only fine-tuning of CatVTON halve the perceptual error on ethnic wear (LPIPS 0.137 to 0.077 on IndoFashion, 0.135 to 0.073 on Atlas; 200 held-out pairs per source) with no regression on Western tops. A two-pass hem-aware mask then removes the remaining failure, recoloured trousers below the hem, on all but 3-4% of pairs at no training cost; in the mirror the hem comes from the previous keyframe for free. The adapted model beats FASHN VTON 1.5 on every aggregate ethnic-wear metric at about $20\times$ lower inference cost, and its weights drop straight into the mirror.

扩散虚拟试穿（VTO）模型能够从单张产品照片生成令人信服的服装迁移效果，但每张图像需要数百毫秒到数秒，使得当今的每一次部署要么是离线的，要么退回到需要为每件产品准备绑定 3D 资产的 AR 试衣镜。我们提出 LiveMirror，一个实时摄像头试穿镜，它在一张 16 GB 消费级 GPU 上使用扩散模型将平面服装照片渲染到运动中的真人身上。其核心是异步关键帧试穿：生成过程从不阻塞显示，每个显示帧都是对最新生成关键帧进行光流扭曲的结果，而关键帧仅通过交叉淡入淡出进行替换。显示以摄像头帧率运行（720p 下 25 FPS），而每 370-490 ms 到达一次新的试穿结果；我们测量残余闪烁，给出逐阶段延迟预算，并报告哪些加速手段（步数、一致性 LoRA、微型解码器、编译）能够保持服装印花完好。然后我们表明，同一张 GPU 还能修复该模型最大的文化盲点：在 VITON-HD 和 DressCode 上训练的试穿模型会将及膝的库尔塔（kurta）或谢尔瓦尼（sherwani）渲染成及躯干长度的上衣，或渲染成裸露双腿上的连衣裙。一个覆盖大腿的掩码、从 24.9k 张模特展示的电商照片自动构建的自监督图像对，以及对 CatVTON 进行 3.2 GPU 小时的仅注意力微调，将民族服饰上的感知误差减半（IndoFashion 上 LPIPS 从 0.137 降至 0.077，Atlas 上从 0.135 降至 0.073；每个来源 200 对留出图像对），且在西式上衣上没有性能回退。随后，一个两遍的下摆感知掩码以零训练成本消除了剩余的失败情况——即下摆以下裤子被重新着色——在除 3-4% 之外的所有图像对上都有效；在试衣镜中，下摆可免费地来自前一个关键帧。适配后的模型在每一项民族服饰聚合指标上都优于 FASHN VTON 1.5，而推理成本约低 $20\times$，并且其权重可直接放入该试衣镜中。

Test-Time Latent Computation to Improve Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models
测试时潜在计算以提升多模态大语言模型的视觉感知
Chen Yang, Zheng Fang, Wenqi Fan, Jun Xia
cs.CV · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Recent work on Large Language Models (LLMs) suggests that reasoning capabilities can be enhanced at test time not only through longer token-level reasoning traces, but also through additional computation in latent space. This raises a natural question for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs): can additional computation in latent space improve visual perception at test time? In this work, we first verify that MLLMs contain stable reusable layers that can be re-forwarded at inference time without disrupting normal generation. Based on this observation, we propose \textbf{Lo}ok \textbf{Ba}ck in the \textbf{L}atent \textbf{S}pace (\textbf{Lobals}), a training-free decoding method that identifies the contiguous layer window with the strongest visual-token attention and re-forwards through it, allowing the model to revisit visual evidence in latent space. We demonstrate that this latent-space revisit strategy can improve MLLMs' performance across diverse multimodal settings, including general vision-language tasks, visual hallucination tasks, and vision-centric tasks.

BEND: Spectral Bregman Losses for Multi-Image Unlearning in Diffusion Models
BEND：用于扩散模型多图像遗忘的谱 Bregman 损失
Mohamed-Hicham Leghettas, Markus Püschel
cs.CV · cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion models memorize training images and reproduce them almost verbatim when prompted, creating copyright and privacy liabilities. Data unlearning erases the influence of specific training samples from a trained model without retraining, and is two-sided: it must forget the targets while preserving generation quality on everything else. Prior methods use the squared-L2 diffusion loss, at most with a hand-set frequency mask; however, it is known that every Bregman divergence is a mathematically valid choice and the squared-L2 is only the simplest example. BEND is the first to search this family: it fits a spectral Bregman divergence to the unlearning task through a bilevel loop, so the loss itself is shaped to forget thoroughly while protecting quality. It also redirects a memorized image to the mean of its retain images, where ReTrack, the state of the art, redirects it to a single near-copy. On Stable Diffusion, a single BEND model erases all 48 verifiably memorized benchmark images at once. It forgets at least as much as per-target, sequential, and jointly trained ReTrack (SSCD 0.084 versus 0.094-0.120), at the quality of the model before unlearning (CLIP-IQA 0.81 versus 0.64-0.69). BEND also outperforms the state of the art on CelebA-HQ in all three measures of the benchmark, and matches or exceeds it on MNIST and CIFAR-10.
Chinese Translation
扩散模型会记住训练图像，并在被提示时几乎逐字地复现它们，从而带来版权和隐私风险。数据遗忘在不重新训练的情况下从已训练模型中抹除特定训练样本的影响，并且具有两面性：它必须遗忘目标样本，同时保持对其他所有内容的生成质量。先前的方法使用平方-L2扩散损失，最多辅以手工设定的频率掩码；然而，已知每种 Bregman 散度都是数学上有效的选择，而平方-L2只是最简单的例子。BEND 首次对该族进行搜索：它通过双层循环为遗忘任务拟合一个谱 Bregman 散度，因此损失本身被塑造为在彻底遗忘的同时保护质量。它还将一张被记住的图像重定向到其保留图像的均值，而当前最先进的方法 ReTrack 将其重定向到单个近副本。在 Stable Diffusion 上，单个 BEND 模型一次性遗忘全部 48 张可验证被记住的基准图像。其遗忘程度至少与逐目标、顺序和联合训练的 ReTrack 相当（SSCD 0.084 对 0.094-0.120），且达到遗忘前模型的质量（CLIP-IQA 0.81 对 0.64-0.69）。BEND 在 CelebA-HQ 上于基准的全部三项指标上均优于当前最先进方法，并在 MNIST 和 CIFAR-10 上达到或超过其表现。

HOSE: Hierarchical Orthogonal Subspace Erasure for Concept Unlearning in Diffusion Models
HOSE：用于扩散模型概念遗忘的分层正交子空间擦除
Xiaoqi Wei, Li Li, Kejiang Chen, Hanzhou Wu, Xinpeng Zhang
cs.CV · cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Text-to-image diffusion models can generate harmful or sensitive content, such as pornographic or violent imagery, raising serious security concerns. Model editing has recently emerged as an efficient approach to mitigate this issue. It modifies pretrained models with minimal parameter updates to alter specific concepts while preserving overall model capabilities. However, due to the entangled representations of different concepts in diffusion models, direct modifications inevitably disrupt non-target concepts. Meanwhile, U-Net's hierarchical heterogeneity hinders unified strategies from balancing erasure and quality. To address these issues, we propose Hierarchical Orthogonal Subspace Erasure (HOSE). This method projects parameter updates into the subspace orthogonal to general knowledge, thereby eliminating interference with non-target concepts. Considering the hierarchical heterogeneity of the U-Net architecture, we further propose a hierarchical adaptive mechanism, constructing differentiated subspace projections for different layers to precisely adapt to the model's hierarchical structure, thereby resolving the inherent trade-off between erasure and image quality in unified constraints. Experimental results demonstrate the proposed method reduces harmful content generation by 80% compared with the unedited model. While it inevitably incurs some image quality degradation, it still outperforms other editing-based baselines in terms of quality preservation, and achieves a significantly better trade-off between harmful content suppression and quality loss than these baselines. Notably, our approach demonstrates higher adversarial robustness than existing SOTA method, indicating that the target concepts have been more thoroughly erased. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/sevenqiiu/HOSE.
Chinese Translation
文生图扩散模型能够生成有害或敏感内容，例如色情或暴力图像，引发严重的安全担忧。模型编辑近来已成为缓解该问题的一种高效方法。它通过最小参数更新修改预训练模型，以改变特定概念，同时保持模型整体能力。然而，由于扩散模型中不同概念的表示相互纠缠，直接修改不可避免地会干扰非目标概念。同时，U-Net 的分层异质性阻碍统一策略在擦除与质量之间取得平衡。为解决这些问题，我们提出分层正交子空间擦除（HOSE）。该方法将参数更新投影到与通用知识正交的子空间中，从而消除对非目标概念的干扰。考虑 U-Net 架构的分层异质性，我们进一步提出一种分层自适应机制，为不同层构建差异化的子空间投影，以精确适应模型的分层结构，从而解决统一约束下擦除与图像质量之间的固有权衡。实验结果表明，与未编辑模型相比，所提方法将有害内容生成减少了 80%。尽管它不可避免地导致一定的图像质量下降，但在质量保持方面仍优于其他基于编辑的基线，并在有害内容抑制与质量损失之间实现了显著优于这些基线的权衡。值得注意的是，我们的方法表现出比现有 SOTA 方法更高的对抗鲁棒性，表明目标概念已被更彻底地擦除。源代码已公开于 https://github.com/sevenqiiu/HOSE。

Auxiliary Clues Aware's Geometry Problem Solving
辅助线索感知的几何问题求解
Qigong Lei, Qingsong Wang, Wang Lin, Qianyi Yang, Chang Yao, Jingyuan Chen
cs.CV · cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Geometry Problem Solving (GPS) serves as a rigorous test of the complex reasoning capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), particularly when solutions require auxiliary constructions absent from the input diagram. However, explicit diagramming methods suffer from unstable image generation quality and cascading errors, while existing implicit attention mechanisms primarily focus on visible elements, limiting their ability to support reasoning that requires additional geometric constructions. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{AuxCA} (Auxiliary-Clues-Aware GRPO), a reinforcement learning framework that helps models learn transferable auxiliary-construction strategies that can be applied beyond the training domain without explicit diagram generation at inference time. Specifically, we introduce Auxiliary Clues Dependency (\textbf{ACD}) to quantify the influence of auxiliary visual clues on token generation and integrate it into GRPO through fine-grained advantage weighting. Furthermore, we incorporate an auxiliary incentive reward to encourage the effective use of auxiliary geometric clues in correct solutions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AuxCA-8B outperforms the explicit-plotting baseline Bagel-Canvas and achieves competitive performance with leading proprietary models on auxiliary-dependent plane geometry problems. Improvements on analytic geometry, solid geometry, and external benchmarks further suggest that the learned strategies can transfer beyond the training domain. Code is available at https://github.com/fukua23/AuxCA
Chinese Translation
几何问题求解（GPS）是对多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）复杂推理能力的严格检验，尤其当解题需要输入图形中不存在的辅助构造时。然而，显式作图方法受制于不稳定的图像生成质量和级联错误，而现有的隐式注意力机制主要关注可见元素，限制了其支持需要额外几何构造的推理的能力。为应对这些挑战，我们提出 \textbf{AuxCA}（Auxiliary-Clues-Aware GRPO），一个强化学习框架，帮助模型学习可迁移的辅助构造策略，这些策略可在推理时无需显式生成图形的情况下应用于训练域之外。具体而言，我们引入辅助线索依赖性（\textbf{ACD}），以量化辅助视觉线索对 token 生成的影响，并通过细粒度的优势加权将其集成到 GRPO 中。此外，我们引入辅助激励奖励，以鼓励在正确解答中有效利用辅助几何线索。大量实验表明，AuxCA-8B 优于显式绘图基线 Bagel-Canvas，并在依赖辅助的平面几何问题上达到与领先专有模型相竞争的性能。在解析几何、立体几何和外部基准上的改进进一步表明，所学策略可以迁移到训练域之外。代码可在 https://github.com/fukua23/AuxCA 获取。

DyLoMo-DiT: Dynamic Looped Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Transformers
DyLoMo-DiT：动态循环混合专家扩散Transformer
Lernie Li, Yuanliu Liu, Pengfei Xiong, Wei Zhang
cs.CV · cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) scale model capacity by increasing both parameter count and computation. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants expand parameter capacity while keeping per-token computation roughly fixed, but still require substantial parameter storage. In this paper, we propose Dynamic Looped MoE DiT (DyLoMo-DiT), which reuses parameters rather than adding them: a weight-shared loop repeatedly applies the middle layers, while sparse experts allocate parameter capacity across tokens. This design deepens the network without adding parameters, freeing the parameter budget for other uses, such as more experts or more distinct layers. It also allocates compute dynamically, varying the number of passes across noise levels. Experiments show that DyLoMo-DiT makes more effective use of parameter and compute budgets, with further gains from assigning more passes to low-noise steps. On ImageNet $256\times256$, DyLoMo-DiT reduces FID by 11-24% relative to DiT and 36-56% relative to DiT-MoE at matched parameter and compute budgets. For text-to-image generation, a scaled DyLoMo-DiT achieves a higher GenEval score than FLUX.1 (0.714 vs. 0.673), with less than one tenth of its active parameters (1.05B vs. 12B).
Chinese Translation
扩散Transformer（DiT）通过同时增加参数数量和计算量来扩展模型容量。混合专家（MoE）变体扩展了参数容量，同时使每个token的计算量大致保持固定，但仍然需要大量的参数存储。在本文中，我们提出动态循环MoE DiT（DyLoMo-DiT），它复用参数而不是增加参数：一个权重共享的循环反复施加中间层，而稀疏专家则在token之间分配参数容量。这种设计在不增加参数的情况下加深了网络，从而将参数预算释放出来用于其他用途，例如更多的专家或更多不同的层。它还能动态分配计算量，在不同噪声水平上改变循环次数。实验表明，DyLoMo-DiT更有效地利用了参数和计算预算，并且将更多循环次数分配给低噪声步骤还能带来进一步的收益。在ImageNet $256\times256$ 上，在参数和计算预算相匹配的情况下，DyLoMo-DiT相较于DiT将FID降低了11-24%，相较于DiT-MoE降低了36-56%。在文本到图像生成方面，一个规模扩展后的DyLoMo-DiT取得了比FLUX.1更高的GenEval分数（0.714对0.673），而其活跃参数不到后者的十分之一（1.05B对12B）。

World Models as Native Latent Action Models
世界模型作为原生潜在动作模型
Qinyue Li, Weijie Qiao, Qingyi Tao, Zerui Gong, Zhe Yang, Quanzhou Li, Taolin Zhang, Jinglin He, Zhonghua Wu, Chen Change Loy
cs.CV · cs.LG · cs.RO
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Large and diverse video sources, such as egocentric human video and heterogeneous robot recordings, carry rich dynamics but come either without actions or without a shared action space. Latent action models (LAMs) can recover these dynamics, but they train their inverse- and forward-dynamics models (IDM, FDM) from scratch, trading off pixel reconstruction against latent capacity and accuracy. Pretrained video world models natively generate high-fidelity dynamics, yet represent them densely, entangled across all layers. Viewing the world model as a LAM, we show that these dynamics can be extracted with minimal changes to the model. Native LAM operates one pretrained video diffusion transformer as both IDM and FDM, with learnable dynamics registers as the only causal bridge between the two, and trains on counterfactual temporal pairs that differ in motion alone, so that the registers distill a video's dynamics into a compact native latent action. We further propose a pretraining paradigm for vision-language-action (VLA) policies, Pretraining Actions from World models (PAWlicy), in which Native LAM serves as a dynamics teacher on large-scale video; unlike world action models, it never generates video. Native latent actions outperform existing LAMs on the LARY benchmark in both action classification and control regression, and replay the same motion on new robots, in new scenes, and from human hands to robots, although no transfer objective is used in training. With a 3.8B model, PAWlicy reaches a 93.6% average success rate on RoboTwin 2.0 trained with domain-randomized demonstrations, the highest among VLAs. On RoboDojo, it is competitive on every dimension we evaluate, and its Precision, evaluated by us, is on par with the leading leaderboard entries. On real robots, it improves over the pi_0.5 baseline on both tasks. Both stages use only public data and a publicly released world model.

cs.LG / 61 / 2611.31163
SPROUT: Predicting Objective-Grounded Prompt Utility for Efficient Text-to-Image Preference Tuning
SPROUT：预测基于目标的提示效用，以实现高效的文本到图像偏好调优
Kangping Hu, Akshay Mehra, Stephen Mussmann
cs.CV · cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Preference tuning of text-to-image diffusion models spends most of its compute generating candidate images, yet training prompts are typically sampled uniformly at random, wasting compute generating images that provide too little signal for model alignment. To best utilize the available compute, we study prompt selection, where at each iteration we identify the most useful prompts for preference tuning. We separate prompt selection into a utility score, an estimator of that utility score, and batch selection. Within this framework, we propose Selection by PRedicting Objective-grounded UTility (SPROUT). The utility score is predicted on every prompt in the pool, including unseen prompts, by a text-only model, refit after every iteration on all utilities observed so far. A randomized acceptance rule then turns these predictions into a batch, so no images are generated beyond those used for training. For direct group preference optimization (DGPO), the objective-grounded utility is the norm of the gradient that the objective produces from a prompt's group of images. Fine-tuning Stable Diffusion 1.5 with DGPO on GenEval, SPROUT matches the final score of uniform sampling in about 44% of the iterations and improves the area under the learning curve with respect to both uniform sampling and CGPO, a recent variance-based prompt sampler. The efficiency gains hold under four held-out reward models never used in training, and the ranking of methods carries over to DPG-Bench and T2I-CompBench++. Our code is available at https://github.com/ADDAPT-ML/SPROUT.

CO-GRAFT: Attributing Reinforcement Learning Gains in Search Agents via Role-Level Policy Grafting

Ramraj Chandradevan, Sayontan Ghosh, Vinoth Selvendran
cs.IR · cs.AI · cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Reinforcement learning (RL) improves large language model search agents by up to 32 exact-match (EM) points over their pre-RL initializations, yet overall accuracy gains do not identify which underlying functional capabilities improve or interact during training. We introduce CO-GRAFT, a reward-agnostic interventional attribution framework in which an RL-trained agent and its pre-RL initialization jointly generate a single trajectory under closed-loop execution with live retrieval. Each policy controls a mutually exclusive subset of four functional roles: intermediate reasoning, search-or-answer decision, search query generation, and final answer extraction. Evaluating all 2^4=16 role assignments without modifying weights or retraining defines a cooperative game whose Shapley values decompose the total RL gain across roles, while M"obius interaction terms distinguish standalone role improvements from multi-role coupling. Applying CO-GRAFT to Search-R1 agents across Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.2 models (spanning two sizes, base and instruction-tuned initializations, GRPO and PPO optimizers, and NQ and HotpotQA datasets), we show that query generation never exceeds 15% of the total gain; instead, gains are governed by pre-RL answer validity, search retention, model scale, and fixed task-level search budgets, shifting credit from reasoning toward answer extraction in larger or well-formatted answer response checkpoints while smaller base models rely on reasoning--decision coupling.

Abstract
Automated electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation has advanced substantially with deep learning, yet many methods remain task-specific and label-dependent. Large language models (LLMs) and time-series foundation models (TSFMs) offer complementary pretrained representations, but integrating them is challenging because of mismatched feature spaces and the lead- and scale-dependent structure of ECG signals. We propose LAF-ECG (Lead-Aware Foundation Fusion for ECG), a dual-foundation framework that extends MedTsLLM with a lead-aware interface to a frozen TSFM backbone while retaining its reprogramming pathway. The proposed framework captures multi-resolution temporal context, fuses temporal and language-aligned ECG representations through adaptive residual integration, and employs branch-specific supervision with cross-branch alignment. LAF-ECG achieves 71.10% accuracy and 62.43% macro-F1 on PTB-XL, and 89.73% accuracy and 65.94% macro-F1 on Chapman-Shaoxing, outperforming MedTsLLM on both datasets. These results highlight the value of preserving lead-specific temporal structure when combining temporal and language foundation representations for ECG classification. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/kkianamm/LAF-ECG.

probly: Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning
probly：不确定性感知机器学习
Paul Hofman, Clemens Damke, Timo Löhr, Santo M. A. R. Thies, Alireza Javanmardi, Valentin Margraf, Jakub Paplham, Yusuf Sale, Eyke Hüllermeier, Maximilian Muschalik
cs.LG · stat.ML
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
As machine learning systems are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, the question of how to represent and quantify uncertainty has moved from a methodological side issue to a central concern. In practice, however, making a model uncertainty-aware is still surprisingly difficult: relevant tools tend to be scattered across libraries, each tied to a particular framework and a particular approach to modeling uncertainty, and the choice of representation, quantification, and evaluation is typically left to the user without much guidance. In this paper, we present probly, a Python package that addresses these issues in a single, modular framework. probly offers (i) lightweight transformations that turn existing models into uncertainty-aware ones, currently supporting PyTorch, scikit-learn, and Flax, (ii) several representations, including second-order distributions, credal sets, and conformal prediction, (iii) the corresponding quantification measures, and (iv) a number of evaluation protocols, which can be combined more or less arbitrarily. Using probly, we conduct a benchmark study on three standard tasks --- selective prediction, out-of-distribution detection, and active learning. In addition, and unlike existing benchmarks, we evaluate suitable methods on first-order data, i.e., datasets for which the target itself is a distribution over outcomes. We further illustrate the flexibility of the package on a number of less standard case studies, including large language models, graph neural networks, and data streams. The package is publicly available at https://github.com/pwhofman/probly.

Selecting Stable Sampling Dynamics for Compositional Diffusion: A Feynman-Kac Weight Reduction
为组合扩散选择稳定采样动力学：一种 Feynman-Kac 权重约简
Sunjin Kim, Sungsoo Ahn, Michael Chertkov
cs.LG · cond-mat.stat-mech · cs.AI · stat.ML
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Given $K$ separately trained diffusion models, how should one sample from a $β_k$-weighted product of their terminal laws without jointly retraining the experts? Existing Feynman--Kac constructions provide many weighted stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with the correct target marginal. The consequential question is how to select useful proposal dynamics among them. We study an explicit family of weighted diffusions that realizes the same product-of-intermediate-experts trajectory. A scalar parameter $λ$ controls how strongly the proposal drift follows the composed expert score, while an additional Langevin component can be varied independently. Writing $B=\sum_{k=1}^{K}β_k>0$, we identify the distinguished choice $λ=1/B$. At this value, the aggregate squared-score term in the instantaneous Feynman--Kac log-weight rate cancels exactly. For positive expert exponents, the remaining score-disagreement contribution is non-positive. We call this structural cancellation Feynman--Kac reduction. Under bounded-divergence assumptions, it yields an upper bound on the instantaneous unnormalized log-weight rate for all $λ\leq 1/B$. For linear diffusion protocols with compactly supported expert data, $λ=1/B$ yields two-sided bounds at every nonterminal time, for exponents of either sign. A corresponding result holds for a single expert under the same divergence assumption. In these two-sided settings, the selected value is unique within the specified family in a universal worst-case sense. Experiments on Gaussian mixtures and molecular sampling compare the analytically predicted stability with actual sampling quality, including instances in which parameter choices different from $λ=1/B$ perform better empirically.

给定 $K$ 个分别训练的扩散模型，如何在不联合重新训练这些专家的情况下，从它们终端分布的 $β_k$ 加权乘积中采样？现有的 Feynman--Kac 构造提供了许多具有正确目标边缘分布的加权随机微分方程（SDEs）。随之而来的问题是，如何在这些动力学中选择有用的提议动力学。我们研究一个显式的加权扩散族，它实现相同的中间专家乘积轨迹。一个标量参数 $λ$ 控制提议漂移跟随组合专家得分的强度，而一个额外的 Langevin 分量可以独立变化。记 $B=\sum_{k=1}^{K}β_k>0$，我们识别出特殊选择 $λ=1/B$。在该取值下，瞬时 Feynman--Kac 对数权重速率中的聚合平方得分项恰好抵消。对于正的专家指数，剩余的得分不一致贡献是非正的。我们将这种结构性的抵消称为 Feynman--Kac 约简。在有界散度假设下，它对所有 $λ\leq 1/B$ 给出瞬时未归一化对数权重速率的上界。对于具有紧支撑专家数据的线性扩散协议，$λ=1/B$ 在每一个非终端时间给出双边界，且对任意符号的指数均成立。在相同的散度假设下，单个专家也有相应的结果。在这些双边设定中，所选值在指定族内于通用最坏情形意义下是唯一的。在高斯混合和分子采样上的实验，将解析预测的稳定性与实际采样质量进行比较，包括那些不同于 $λ=1/B$ 的参数选择在经验上表现更好的情形。

diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Conditional generation under constraints that can only be checked on a finished sample, such as a molecular property filter, remains challenging for diffusion models: most guidance methods require differentiable measurement operators, paired conditional data, or rollouts of the base model at every step. We present a framework grounded in the Doob $h$-transform that reduces conditional generation to learning a single function, the probability that a noisy sample denoises into the constraint set. We learn this function from binary clean-sample evaluations alone, by squared-error regression on forward-noised labels; the base model is frozen, one lightweight head is trained per constraint, and noisy-state classifier guidance arises as a special case. The exact guidance step fades where the constraint signal provably vanishes and carries a factor of the inverse probability across samples, which normalized guidance discards: with the schedule and mean step size held fixed, equalizing the step costs 17.0 to 18.5 points of constraint satisfaction on CIFAR-10 at comparable FID, across independently trained estimators. Guidance is more than 50$\times$ cheaper per satisfying sample than rejection sampling at a 1.7% base rate, raises a Lipinski-type property filter on QM9 from 54.3% to 96.8%, and lifts satisfaction on Stable Diffusion 1.5 from 7.2% to 60.0% at one sixteenth of the cost of derivative-free selection, which reaches 9.0%. These results demonstrate that binary evaluations of clean samples are sufficient supervision for constrained generation across pixel, latent, and molecular diffusion.

Abstract
Individual heterogeneity and acquisition-site variability complicate neuroimaging-based characterization of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We propose PsyDrift, combining ASD/healthy-control-supervised functional-connectivity representations with healthy-reference latent diffusion. An encoder produces 128-dimensional representations, and a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) learns exclusively from healthy training latents. The classifier and DDPM achieve mean-site AUROCs of $0.798 \pm 0.003$ and $0.718 \pm 0.013$, respectively; uncertainties denote seed standard deviations. Matched healthy-reference scorers on the same representation achieve 0.68-0.71; the statistical significance of diffusion's modest numerical advantage remains unestablished. Within ASD, scores show weak associations with ADOS Total (Spearman $ρ= 0.108$, $p = 0.038$) and full-scale IQ ($ρ= -0.138$, $p = 0.002$), without adjustment for age, sex, site, or head motion. cs.LG / 68 / 2611.30153
IADR: Interface-Augmented Neural Operator for Phase-Field Mean-Curvature Flow
IADR：面向相场平均曲率流的界面增强神经算子
Qinyi Zhang, Duanyu Feng, Yangshuai Wang, Hao Wang
cs.LG · math.NA
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
The Allen-Cahn equation is one of the standard phase-field models for mean-curvature flow (MCF), parameterised by the diffuse-interface width $\varepsilon$. Practical simulations span a range of $\varepsilon$, so a single model covering this range is needed. PDE-specific neural operators are accurate but must be retrained at every $\varepsilon$; general neural operators cover $\varepsilon$ in one model but lose the phase-field structure of the target. We introduce Interface-Augmented Diffusion-Reaction (IADR), a neural operator that addresses both shortcomings: a target network with a diffusion-and-reaction (DR) structure preserves the phase-field structure of the Allen-Cahn equation, while a hypernetwork that maps $\varepsilon$ to the weights of this target network amortises the dependence on $\varepsilon$ across the range. A single IADR matches the per-$\varepsilon$ specialists on in-distribution data within the prescribed range, retains their cross-shape generalisation under both $\varepsilon$- and geometry-out-of-distribution shifts, and retains their compact DR target structure with millisecond-scale inference. We further establish a conditional $K$-step rollout error bound under consistency and stability assumptions.

Learning Teacher Output Preferences from Final Responses for Reasoning Distillation
从最终响应中学习教师输出偏好以进行推理蒸馏
Hongli Shen, Shaopeng Fu, Qinbo Zhang, Jian Li, Di Wang
cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Many large language models (LLMs) use chain-of-thought (CoT) to solve complex problems, but hide their CoT traces to prevent reasoning capabilities from being distilled. While recent studies have shown that hidden CoTs can be reconstructed, existing methods typically require training a separate attacker for each target LLM. This paper studies model-agnostic CoT reconstruction, aiming to reconstruct hidden CoT traces from arbitrary target LLMs using only input prompts and visible final responses. We propose Final-Output Preference Learning (FOPL), which trains a single reconstruction model that generalizes to unseen LLMs without target-specific adaptation. To achieve this, the reconstruction model must learn which reasoning patterns match a given final response without knowing the target LLM's identity. We address this using preference optimization, training the reconstruction model to prefer native CoTs over synthetic alternatives for the same question and final response. By learning these preferences from LLMs with accessible CoTs, the reconstruction model learns to distinguish reasoning patterns based on visible responses. Experiments show that reconstructed CoTs capture distinct reasoning patterns across LLM families, including a family unseen during training. Moreover, students trained on reconstructed CoTs match or outperform those trained on native CoTs across several reasoning benchmarks.
Chinese Translation
许多大语言模型（LLM）使用思维链（CoT）来求解复杂问题，但会隐藏其 CoT 轨迹，以防止推理能力被蒸馏。尽管近期研究表明隐藏的 CoT 可以被重建，但现有方法通常需要为每个目标 LLM 训练一个单独的攻击者。本文研究模型无关的 CoT 重建，旨在仅利用输入提示和可见的最终响应，从任意目标 LLM 中重建隐藏的 CoT 轨迹。我们提出最终输出偏好学习（Final-Output Preference Learning, FOPL），它训练单个重建模型，该模型无需针对特定目标进行适配即可泛化到未见过的 LLM。为实现这一点，重建模型必须在不知道目标 LLM 身份的情况下，学习哪些推理模式与给定的最终响应相匹配。我们通过偏好优化来解决这一问题，训练重建模型对于同一问题和最终响应更偏好原生 CoT 而非合成替代方案。通过从 CoT 可访问的 LLM 中学习这些偏好，重建模型学会基于可见响应来区分推理模式。实验表明，重建的 CoT 能够捕捉跨 LLM 系列的不同推理模式，包括训练期间未见过的一个系列。此外，在多个推理基准上，使用重建 CoT 训练的学生模型与使用原生 CoT 训练的学生模型表现相当或更优。

cs.LG / 70 / 2611.30405
Optimistic Online Learning for Coding Agents with Aggregate Feedback
面向编码智能体的带聚合反馈的乐观在线学习
Hao Luan, Hao Qiu, Zhi Zheng, See-Kiong Ng, Zhiyong Huang
cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) coding agents operating on Web development platforms can interact with repositories, issue trackers, and continuous integration services to carry out long-horizon software engineering tasks. However, behavioral drift remains a major bottleneck in such multi-turn reasoning and action trajectories. To mitigate this, activation steering has emerged as a promising approach for regularizing agent behaviors by intervening on the LLM's transformer residual streams. Nonetheless, existing methods typically apply a static steering policy across all tasks, overlooking the fact that a single policy is rarely effective across heterogeneous tasks and varying execution turns. This limitation motivates dynamic online selection among candidate steering policies. Yet, doing so in long-horizon agentic settings is challenging: verifiable task-level feedback is only revealed upon task completion, leaving the contributions of individual steering turns unobserved. To address this challenge, we formulate online steering-policy selection as a multi-armed bandit problem with delayed task-level feedback and turn-level predictive hints derived from residual-stream activations. Within this formulation, we introduce Online Optimistic Activation Steering, a meta-framework that uses hints to guide within-task steering policy selection and leverages terminal task-level feedback to correct cumulative reward estimates. Theoretically, against the best fixed policy in hindsight, we prove regret bounds that tighten with increasing hint accuracy and establish a matching lower bound with respect to prediction error and candidate policy count. Empirical evaluations on realistic coding benchmarks demonstrate that our framework outperforms both static steering policies and naive online adaptive baselines.
Chinese Translation
在Web开发平台上运行的大语言模型（LLM）编码智能体可以与代码仓库、问题跟踪器和持续集成服务交互，以执行长时程软件工程任务。然而，行为漂移仍然是此类多轮推理与动作轨迹中的主要瓶颈。为缓解这一问题，激活引导已作为一种有前景的方法出现，通过干预LLM的Transformer残差流来正则化智能体行为。尽管如此，现有方法通常对所有任务应用静态引导策略，忽略了单一策略很少能在异构任务和变化的执行轮次中有效这一事实。这一局限促使在候选引导策略之间进行动态在线选择。然而，在长时程智能体设置中这样做具有挑战性：可验证的任务级反馈仅在任务完成时才揭示，导致各个引导轮次的贡献无法被观测。为应对这一挑战，我们将在线引导策略选择建模为一个多臂老虎机问题，该问题具有延迟的任务级反馈以及由残差流激活导出的轮次级预测提示。在这一建模框架内，我们引入在线乐观激活引导（Online Optimistic Activation Steering），这是一个元框架，它利用提示来指导任务内引导策略选择，并利用终端任务级反馈来校正累积奖励估计。在理论上，针对事后最佳固定策略，我们证明了随提示准确性提高而收紧的遗憾界，并建立了关于预测误差和候选策略数量的匹配下界。在真实编码基准上的实证评估表明，我们的框架优于静态引导策略和朴素的在线自适应基线。

cs.LG / 71 / 2611.30605
Vasicek Diffusion Bridge for Graph Generation
用于图生成的 Vasicek 扩散桥
Junyi Tang, Chang Liu, Kun Zhan
cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion-based graph generation models progressively transform Gaussian noise into structured graphs through stochastic dynamics. We observe that the effectiveness of this transformation is fundamentally determined by the evolution of the diffusion trajectory. Existing graph diffusion models often suffer from excessive uncertainty during diffusion and delayed growth of the signal-to-noise ratio, causing useful structural information to emerge only in the later stages of generation. To address this issue, we propose the Vasicek Graph Diffusion (VGD), a graph diffusion process derived from the Vasicek dynamics. The key insight of VGD is data-anchored mean dynamics with a closed-form solution, which analytically establishes a continuous transition from Gaussian noise to the target graph distribution. Unlike conventional graph diffusion processes that rely predominantly on stochastic evolution, VGD introduces a data-anchored drift that continuously steers the latent state toward the target distribution throughout diffusion. As a consequence, VGD maintains a smoothly evolving uncertainty while rapidly increasing the signal-to-noise ratio throughout diffusion, allowing informative graph structures to emerge much earlier during generation. Extensive experiments on multiple graph generation benchmarks demonstrate that VGD outperforms existing diffusion-based graph generative models in terms of generation quality and structural fidelity.
Chinese Translation
基于扩散的图生成模型通过随机动力学逐步将高斯噪声转换为结构化图。我们观察到，这种转换的有效性从根本上由扩散轨迹的演化决定。现有图扩散模型常常在扩散过程中遭受过大的不确定性以及信噪比的延迟增长，导致有用的结构信息仅在生成的后期阶段才出现。为解决这一问题，我们提出 Vasicek 图扩散（VGD），一种源自 Vasicek 动力学的图扩散过程。VGD 的关键洞见是具有闭式解的数据锚定均值动力学，它在解析上建立了从高斯噪声到目标图分布的连续过渡。与传统图扩散过程主要依赖随机演化不同，VGD 引入数据锚定漂移，在扩散全程持续将潜状态引向目标分布。因此，VGD 在扩散全程保持平滑演化的不确定性，同时快速提高信噪比，使得有信息量的图结构在生成过程中更早出现。在多个图生成基准上的大量实验表明，VGD 在生成质量和结构保真度方面优于现有基于扩散的图生成模型。

Uncovering the Tells: Efficient Black-Box Audits for LLM Data Contamination
揭示线索：面向大语言模型数据污染的高效黑盒审计
Dominik Bernard Lau, Filip Pawlicki, Jan Dubiński, Sebastian Cygert
cs.LG · cs.AI · cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Existing methods for assessing training data contamination in Large Language Models achieve high accuracy, but fundamentally rely on gray-box access, rendering them inapplicable to fully black-box environments. This limitation forces auditors to rely on full-sequence sampling or rigid heuristics, both of which incur prohibitive inference costs and struggle to isolate the underlying memorization signal. To overcome this, we propose a generation-based black-box framework that infers context-induced information gain from targeted token discrepancies. We introduce a budget-constrained auditing regime, building on the empirical observation that the membership signal is highly sparse and concentrated in a few highly informative tokens. We formalize this sparsity, showing why uniform sampling needs many more samples than a policy that targets informative positions. Empirically, our approach achieves state-of-the-art black-box separation accuracy while needing about 3x fewer queries than uniform position sampling. Finally, we apply this methodology to closed frontier models, exploring its capacity and limits in surfacing potential training data overlaps on commercial APIs.
Chinese Translation
现有用于评估大语言模型训练数据污染的方法虽能达到较高准确率，但在根本上依赖灰盒访问，这使其无法适用于完全黑盒的环境。这一局限迫使审计人员依赖全序列采样或僵化的启发式方法，而两者都会带来高昂得令人却步的推理成本，并且难以分离出潜在的记忆信号。为克服这一问题，我们提出一种基于生成的黑盒框架，该框架从有针对性的 token 差异中推断由上下文引起的信息增益。我们引入一种预算受限的审计机制，其建立在以下经验观察之上：成员资格信号高度稀疏，并集中于少数信息量很高的 token 中。我们对这种稀疏性进行了形式化，说明为什么均匀采样比针对信息性位置的策略需要多得多的样本。在实证上，我们的方法在实现最先进的黑盒区分准确率的同时，所需查询次数比均匀位置采样少约 3 倍。最后，我们将这一方法应用于闭源前沿模型，探索其在商业 API 上揭示潜在训练数据重叠的能力与局限。

Evaluable Language-Model Treatment Policies for Sepsis Resuscitation via Offline Value-Guided Selection
通过离线价值引导选择实现可评估的语言模型脓毒症复苏治疗策略
Yue Pei, Shining Bo, Yingying Zhang, Qinggang Ge, Zhiling Zhao, Jian Cheng, Haogang Zhu
cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Offline treatment learning must balance imitation, which stays close to logged evidence but ignores outcomes, against value maximisation, which uses outcomes but drifts toward treatments the records cannot verify. Numerical reinforcement learning strikes this balance during training. For large language models (LLMs), directly using sparse retrospective outcomes for fine-tuning raises challenges of delayed credit assignment and limited evidence for alternative treatments. We present R-LLMC, which strikes the balance at inference for sepsis resuscitation. A behaviour-supervised LLM, decoded into an exact distribution over 25 vasopressor-fluid actions, proposes clinician-anchored candidates; an offline critic selects among them by estimated long-term value. The policy has a closed form for off-policy evaluation, and its rationale is written after selection, so explanation cannot steer treatment. In experiments on held-out MIMIC-III patients, R-LLMC exceeded the clinician reference in doubly robust value by +0.214 (95\% CI 0.091-0.300), with fitted Q evaluation agreeing.

离线治疗学习必须在模仿与价值最大化之间取得平衡：模仿贴近记录中的证据但忽略结局，而价值最大化利用结局但会漂向记录无法验证的治疗。数值强化学习在训练过程中实现这种平衡。对于大语言模型（LLM）而言，直接使用稀疏的回顾性结局进行微调会带来延迟信用分配以及替代治疗证据有限等挑战。我们提出 R-LLMC，它在推理阶段为脓毒症复苏实现这种平衡。一个经行为监督的 LLM 被解码为 25 种血管加压药-液体动作上的精确分布，它提出以临床医生为锚点的候选方案；一个离线评论家根据估计的长期价值在其中进行选择。该策略具有用于离策略评估的闭式形式，且其理由是在选择之后写出的，因此解释无法操纵治疗。在留出的 MIMIC-III 患者上的实验中，R-LLMC 在双重稳健价值上超过临床医生参考值 +0.214（95\% CI 0.091-0.300），拟合 Q 评估结果与之相符。

cs.LG / 74 / 2611.30986
Reinforcing Diffusion Models by Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching
通过瞬时轨迹分布匹配强化扩散模型
Yihong Luo
cs.LG · cs.AI · cs.CV
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Forward diffusion reinforcement learning (RL)---enabling deterministic ODE sampling without trajectory backpropagation---has grown increasingly popular for efficiently aligning diffusion models. However, we reveal that existing methods essentially rely on signed reward-weighted regression (RWR), regressing the \emph{trainable policy} velocity onto rollouts from a \emph{behavior distribution}. Unbiased baseline subtraction implicitly assumes that the policy velocity equals the behavior marginal velocity---an idealized assumption violated under classifier-free guidance (CFG) rollouts, offline/off-policy updates, and imperfect online self-consistency. This \emph{behavior--policy mismatch} breaks baseline invariance and injects \emph{baseline-induced gradient drift}, destabilizing training. To resolve this issue, we propose \textbf{I}nstantaneous \textbf{T}rajectory \textbf{D}istribution \textbf{M}atching (\textbf{iTDM}), taking the infinitesimal limit of Trajectory Distribution Matching toward a time-local reward-guided target via the posterior-score identity to yield a sample-level gradient anchored at the behavior velocity without learning an additional reward-tilted target score. Tracking this velocity with an online auxiliary denoiser guarantees exact baseline invariance at the auxiliary optimum, effectively suppressing baseline drift across both online and offline RL. Extensive experiments across compositional generation, text rendering, and preference alignment show that iTDM achieves state-of-the-art in-domain and out-of-domain performance. Notably, on the challenging GenEval2 benchmark, iTDM converges nearly $3\times$ faster than competing methods while scaling smoothly to $0.87$ without collapse. Code is available at https://github.com/Luo-Yihong/iTDM
Chinese Translation
前向扩散强化学习（RL）——使确定性 ODE 采样无需轨迹反向传播——在高效对齐扩散模型方面正变得越来越流行。然而，我们揭示出现有方法本质上依赖带符号的奖励加权回归（RWR），将可训练策略的速度回归到来自行为分布的 rollout 上。无偏基线减除隐含地假设策略速度等于行为边缘速度——这一理想化假设在无分类器引导（CFG）rollout、离线/离策略更新以及不完美的在线自一致性下会被违背。这种行为—策略不匹配破坏了基线不变性，并注入由基线引起的梯度漂移，使训练不稳定。为解决该问题，我们提出瞬时轨迹分布匹配（iTDM），通过后验分数恒等式取轨迹分布匹配朝向时间局部奖励引导目标的无穷小极限，以产生锚定在行为速度上的样本级梯度，而无需学习额外的奖励倾斜目标分数。利用在线辅助去噪器跟踪该速度，在辅助最优处保证精确的基线不变性，从而有效抑制在线和离线 RL 中的基线漂移。在组合生成、文本渲染和偏好对齐上的大量实验表明，iTDM 在域内和域外性能上均达到最先进水平。值得注意的是，在具有挑战性的 GenEval2 基准上，iTDM 的收敛速度比竞争方法快近 $3\times$，同时平滑扩展到 $0.87$ 且不崩溃。代码见 https://github.com/Luo-Yihong/iTDM

Site-Conditioned Boundary Closure for Subsurface Seepage Forecasting and Relief Placement
用于地下渗流预测与减压布置的场地条件化边界闭合
Edward Holmberg, Elias Ioup, Mahdi Abdelguerfi
cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Truncating a large heterogeneous diffusion model around a localized, threshold-activated outlet saves degrees of freedom but severs exterior feedback that governs when the outlet opens and how much it discharges. By separating forcing-driven background head from local withdrawal drawdown, Site-Conditioned Boundary Closure (SCBC) maps local physical descriptors to positive exchange coefficients at the cut boundary. Supervised on unforced donor-domain withdrawal responses, these coefficients yield a passivity-preserving reduced operator that generalizes across unseen forcing histories without refitting. We evaluate SCBC on flood-driven subsurface seepage beneath levee foundations against full-grid reference simulations (MODFLOW~6). Across three held-out foundation panels, a single frozen SCBC tree estimator reduced peak-discharge log RMSE by 26.1%, 30.9% and 42.6% relative to identical local patches using a shared boundary coefficient. We then test whether better screening forecasts improve constrained placement, minimizing peak landside toe head subject to a discharge capacity limit and a budget of three sequential full-grid checks. On a separate 36-foundation test using a coarser 30-state ring operator, a neural SCBC estimator improved discharge forecasts across candidates yet selected four over-capacity placements before checks, compared with one for a shared-coefficient ring, which recovered all 144 reference optima after three checks.

cs.LG / 76 / 2611.31166
Precision-Aware Learning Rate Transfer Across Block Count in LLM Post-Training
大语言模型后训练中跨块数量的精度感知学习率迁移
Nan Chen, Soledad Villar, Soufiane Hayou
cs.LG · cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
The post-training of pretrained large language models, including supervised finetuning (SFT), direct preference optimization (DPO), and reinforcement learning with verifiable reward (RLVR), is very sensitive to the learning rate, and tuning it through grid search is costly in both computation and memory. In this work, we propose \textbf{TipSweep}, a method to transfer the learning rate across the number of trainable transformer blocks. To do so efficiently, we search for the best learning rate by training only the last $k_0$ blocks (in our experiments, typically $k_0=1$), and provide scaling rules that predict the optimal learning rate when training any set of $k$ blocks, including when $k=L$ (the full transformer). Across experiments with models ranging from 1 to 7 billion parameters, we observe that the optimal learning rate follows precision-dependent scaling rules: the optimal rate scales approximately as $k^{-1}$ with float32 (FP32) master weights, but as $k^{-1/2}$ when updates are applied directly to bfloat16 (BF16) weights without a master copy. We explain both rules using an analytical model that accounts for update rounding, under assumptions supported by profiling experiments. Finally, we develop two prototypes of the learning rate search for a 6.7-billion-parameter model. The first fits the search on a single consumer GPU with 16 GiB of memory. The second speeds up the search on a high-end GPU by evaluating all candidate learning rates in a single pass over the data, so that a five-candidate search takes about half the GPU hours of one full-depth ($k=L$) run.
Chinese Translation
预训练大语言模型的后训练，包括监督微调（SFT）、直接偏好优化（DPO）和带可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR），对学习率非常敏感，而通过网格搜索调优学习率在计算和内存上代价高昂。在这项工作中，我们提出\textbf{TipSweep}，一种跨可训练Transformer块数量迁移学习率的方法。为了高效地做到这一点，我们仅训练最后$k_0$个块（在我们的实验中，通常$k_0=1$）来搜索最佳学习率，并提供缩放规则，用于预测在训练任意$k$个块集合时的最优学习率，包括当$k=L$（完整Transformer）时。在参数规模从10亿到70亿的模型实验中，我们观察到最优学习率遵循依赖于精度的缩放规则：在使用float32（FP32）主权重时，最优学习率大致按$k^{-1}$缩放，但当更新直接应用于没有主副本的bfloat16（BF16）权重时，则按$k^{-1/2}$缩放。我们使用一个考虑更新舍入的分析模型来解释这两条规则，该模型基于性能分析实验支持的假设。最后，我们为67亿参数模型开发了两种学习率搜索原型。第一种将搜索适配到具有16 GiB内存的单张消费级GPU上。第二种在高档GPU上通过对数据的一次遍历评估所有候选学习率来加速搜索，因此五候选搜索所耗GPU小时数约为一次全深度（$k=L$）运行的一半。

From Local Errors to System Failures: Modeling and Benchmarking Error Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
从局部错误到系统失效：多智能体 LLM 系统中错误传播的建模与基准测试
Wenlong Yu, Bingxu Lu, Qilong Wang, Qinghua Hu, Qianru Sun
cs.MA · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
In multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models (LLMs), errors can propagate through intermediate messages and compromise final answers. However, outcome-based evaluation obscures how agents amplify, attenuate, or correct these errors. We propose Response-Aware Error Propagation among Agents (REPA), a structural model that connects measured local responses to system-level error propagation. REPA separately estimates input assembly and agent processing across multiple error channels, while theoretical analysis relates local modeling errors to endpoint prediction error. Experiments span three Qwen base models, six MAS workflows, and ten knowledge and reasoning settings in ErrPropBench-10. REPA achieves a mean condition-level Spearman correlation of 0.84 across base models, compared with 0.47 for direct regression. Controlled experiments also demonstrate its utility for targeted recovery. REPA-guided retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves accuracy over no retrieval by an average of 19 percentage points with 16% additional tokens. By linking local agent behavior to system susceptibility, REPA provides an interpretable foundation for studying error propagation and developing targeted optimization in MAS.

Abstract
Safety-critical scenarios are rare in recorded driving and must be generated to test and train motion planners of automated vehicles. In guided diffusion models, each scenario type needs its own weighted objective, separate from the validity check. Optimized together with the attacker, the vehicle under test can cancel the attack or draw it toward itself. We state each scenario as a signal temporal logic specification with clauses typed by role. Every clause names the agent it may change and the agents it may read, and the vehicle under test reads the attacker only from the attack onset. A large language model drafts the specification from a description, and a type checker accepts it. A compiler derives the optimization: it edits a diffusion model's samples by the smallest change that satisfies the specification, each clause moves only its owner, the attacker is solved against the unreacted vehicle under test before its response, and the monitor of the same specification decides acceptance. On nuScenes and CommonRoad, judged independently of the specification, one parameter set produced valid scenarios at a rate 0.14 above a weighted objective tuned per scenario type, and descriptions yielded at least one valid scenario for 11 of the 16 pre-crash types expressible in the public data. Learned planners fail more often on the generated scenarios than on their seeds. Fine-tuning on them lowers a planner's failure rate on critical scenarios, and the time headway one clause of the label requires, not the generator, sets the size of the gain.

Skill-Adaptive Noise Scheduling for Diffusion Policies
面向扩散策略的技能自适应噪声调度
Woo Kyung Kim, Gwangpyo Yoo, Eunyoung Park, Honguk Woo
cs.RO · cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Recent advances in diffusion policies have demonstrated strong effectiveness when integrated into hierarchical skill-based learning frameworks, leveraging offline data to capture multimodal and temporally abstracted behaviors. However, prior approaches have rarely considered the diffusion process as a learnable component, adopting fixed noise schedules applied uniformly across skills, regardless of their distinct behavioral contexts. Such a design fundamentally limits the achievable performance, particularly for contact-rich and dexterous manipulation tasks where different skills exhibit distinct couplings between action dimensions. In this paper, we present a skill-adaptive noise diffusion framework (SaND) which introduces a learnable, skill-conditioned noise schedule that modulates the diffusion process per action dimension, adapting the noising dynamics to each skill. To prevent the learned noise schedule from collapsing into trivial solutions, we employ an auxiliary inverse objective that reconstructs the skill embedding from the Legendre coefficients of the derivative of the noise schedule, encouraging the schedules to remain skill-discriminative. This formulation naturally enables adaptive control over the denoising steps for each skill, where noise schedules are clustered in the Legendre coefficient space, and the appropriate number of denoising steps is determined at the point where reconstruction error abruptly increases. At inference, we identify each skill embedding's cluster from its noise schedule and apply the corresponding number of denoising steps, dedicating more compute to skills requiring fine-grained control and less to simpler ones. In simulation and on real robot hardware, SaND outperforms existing skill learning and planning baselines on contact-rich and dexterous manipulation tasks, achieving higher success rates while requiring fewer denoising steps.

Admitted Is Not Effective: Lessons from a Notary-Gated Retrospective Loop in an Agentic Pipeline
准入并不等于有效：来自智能体流水线中公证门控回顾循环的经验教训
Lo Gullstrand Heander, Emma Söderberg, Christofer Rydenfält
cs.SE · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Agentic software development pipelines with frozen prompts can repeat the same mistakes across pull requests (PRs), yet ungoverned additions to instruction files grow without bound and do not generally improve task success. We present a retrospective loop for a four-stage large language model (LLM) pipeline in which a Retrospective agent proposes edits to learned rules every ten PRs and a Notary admits, merges, or rejects them while recording each decision in a provenance ledger. In a pre-registered study of 880 PRs on two Python repositories, the loop ran end to end and the Notary admitted 55 of 89 proposals, rejecting 8 that cited nonexistent evidence. However, held-out review comments and hidden-test resolution did not improve after ten retrospectives. Tracing each step of the loop, we found that sparse review signal (0.45 comments/PR) left little to learn from and that rules admitted on their stated evidence did not show measurable held-out effects. We derive six lessons and argue that governed loops should admit and retire every learned rule as a testable hypothesis.

Can Vibe Coding Produce Accessible Websites: An Empirical Study on LLM Coding Agents and Skills

Syed Fatiul Huq, Md. Asif Haider, Abu Jafar Saifullah, Thomas Zimmermann, Sam Malek
cs.SE · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) coding agents increasingly allow developers and non-professionals to create websites through natural-language instructions, with limited inspection of the generated source code. Although this ``vibe coding'' workflow lowers barriers to software creation, it may also propagate accessibility defects at scale. We investigate the accessibility of websites generated end-to-end by contemporary coding agents and whether agent-level accessibility interventions improve their output. We generated 90 websites for three projects using combinations of three coding agents, four language models, and multiple reasoning-effort levels. We evaluated complete interaction journeys using axe-core, IBM Equal Access Accessibility Checker, and QualWeb, and converged reports to observe violation prevalence and violated WCAG Success Criterion (SC). None of the 90 baseline websites was fully accessible, with an average of 80.43 violated interface elements. 13 WCAG SCs were violated at least once across the runs. Color contrast was the most prevalent issue, followed by labeling, semantic-structure, keyboard, and visualization failures. We reran 24 matched configurations with a general accessibility Skill and a contrast-specific Skill. Both significantly improved accessibility scores, but neither eliminated violations. User testing with blind individuals corroborated the experiential effects of the detected inaccessibilities. Moreover, functional correctness decreased with the inclusion of Skills. Our findings show that accessibility does not reliably emerge from vibe coding, and agentic interventions can both improve some accessibility issues and introduce new functional ones.

large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Advancements in large language models (LLMs) have enhanced their ability to handle ambiguous user instructions. However, effective prompt patterns remain crucial for usability and comprehension. This article presents a taxonomy of prompt engineering patterns for software engineering. It is based on a systematic literature review that was conducted in early 2023, when LLMs still faced significant limitations in context length and inference capabilities. Our study explores techniques that enhance the usability and reliability of LLMs, emphasizing the ongoing importance of well-designed prompts in optimizing task performance. Our findings highlight the critical role of prompt patterns in maximizing LLM's potential, even as their capabilities continue to evolve.

LLM-Assisted Software Migration: from Module-Level Transformation to Repository-Level Integration
LLM辅助的软件迁移：从模块级转换到仓库级集成
Yanan Zhang, Shengqi Liu, Tao Zhang, Yidi Liu, Alan Tang, Hailong Chen, Yantao Jia
cs.SE · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Software migration adapts an existing implementation to a new language, version, API, framework, or platform while preserving its behavior. Large language models (LLMs) succeed on individual functions and modules, but this success does not readily carry over to entire repositories, particularly deployable applications. This survey reviews LLM-assisted migration from module-level transformation to repository-level integration, culminating in the delivery of complete applications. We analyze 96 sources---including 46 direct migration papers---across four perspectives: (1) supported software engineering activities, (2) model roles as editors or orchestrators, (3) orchestration workflows (agentless, single-agent, or multi-agent), and (4) enabling techniques including knowledge engineering, project context, environment feedback, and model adaptation. We then compare evaluation practices and benchmarks. Although 30 of the 46 studies target repositories, most acceptance evidence relies merely on build success, supplied tests, or static and model-based proxies. Moreover, compilation, visual similarity, test outcomes, and runtime behavior capture fundamentally distinct properties and cannot be conflated into a single success rate. We also identify critical gaps in requirements engineering support and in controlled comparisons of agent architectures. Finally, we discuss six open problems: application integration, platform differences, non-functional properties, generalization, attribution of gains, as well as cost and maintenance.

RepoClean: Evaluating Coding Agents on Repository-Level Obsolete Code Cleanup
RepoClean：评估编码智能体在仓库级过时代码清理中的表现
Hongyixuan Yuan, Qixing Zhou, Pengcheng Huang, Qingshuo Ni, Runsong Zhao, Shaokai He, Xiangpeng Li, Deqiang Ouyang
cs.SE · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) agents have demonstrated strong repository-level programming capabilities. However, as software evolves, repository code may become redundant or obsolete, increasing maintenance costs and potentially introducing functional issues. Agents must therefore identify and remove unnecessary code safely, yet autonomous repository-level code cleanup remains insufficiently evaluated in isolation. To evaluate this capability, we introduce RepoClean, a benchmark of 200 cleanup tasks from 34 popular open-source Python repositories. RepoClean is constructed by automatically reintroducing deleted code from real repository histories into newer versions, preserving current implementations and retaining instances where previously passing tests consequently fail. To restore existing functionality without new feature development, agents must use repository interfaces and cross-file dependencies to determine which historical code to remove and which implementations to preserve. Evaluation of seven models shows that even the best-performing model, GPT-6 Astra, resolves only 23% of tasks. Further analysis reveals that agents remove substantially less obsolete code when cleanup is not explicitly requested. RepoClean provides a foundation for systematically studying these cleanup challenges and advancing coding agents toward autonomous software maintenance.

Useful but Unwieldy: How Software Engineers Perceive the Design of Chain-of-Thought Explanations in Coding Agents
